1	# Claim to Fame engine — architecture
2	
3	The challenge brief is in `GAME_DESCRIPTION.md`, the API in `API_HANDBOOK.md`.
4	Code lives in `c2f/`, tests in `tests/`, per-game logs in `runs/`.
5	
6	## One command per game
7	
8	```
9	make 7          # play game 7: wait for key → decrypt → extract → model → price → submit
10	make check      # real model against the permanent test game 0
11	make test       # unit tests
12	```
13	
14	Start `make N` a few seconds before the game opens. `get_case.sh` polls the key endpoint
15	every 0.3 s; the 60-second clock starts when the key appears. Everything must be submitted
16	within that minute. Last write wins on the server.
17	
18	## Pipeline
19	
20	```
21	IN              EXTRACT            MODEL                 PRICE              OUT
22	cases/NN.zip    extract.py         llm.py                price.py           submit.py
23	+ key   ──►     case dict   ──►    one LLM call   ──►    (a, b) per item ──► PUT /submissions
24	get_case.sh     policy text        covered? related?     a = charge         runs/game_NN.json
25	                description text   t_low/mid/high        b = accept limit
26	                invoice rows       clause + reason
27	                image names
28	```
29	
30	| Step | Module | Input | Output |
31	|---|---|---|---|
32	| IN | `get_case.sh` | `cases/case_NN.zip`, `GET /api/games/NN/key` | `cases/case_NN/` |
33	| EXTRACT | `c2f/extract.py` | policy.txt, description.txt, invoices.pdf, *.png | case dict (below) |
34	| DIGEST | `c2f/policy.py` | policy.txt | `policy_digest`: limits / deductibles / exclusions |
35	| MODEL | `c2f/llm.py` | case dict + system prompt | JSON: per item covered, related, clause, t_low/t_mid/t_high, t_if_covered, reason; policy_summary |
36	| PRICE | `c2f/price.py` | model JSON | `[{index, charge_price, acceptance_limit}]` |
37	| OUT | `c2f/submit.py` | rows | `PUT /api/games/NN/submissions`, log in `runs/` |
38	
39	`c2f/run.py` orchestrates. **One pass**, on one model (`gpt-5.6-terra` everywhere). Its
40	timeout is whatever is left of the ~53 s clock (floor `MIN_MODEL_S`); the invoice is split into
41	`ceil(n / C2F_CHUNK_ITEMS)` parallel calls (10 items → 1, 20 → 2, 32 → 4, capped at
42	`C2F_MAX_CHUNKS`) so a slow chunk costs only its own rows, and every submission still carries
43	the full row set. Because one model and one pass free up the call budget, the pass runs at
44	`reasoning_effort` **medium**: 29 items in 12 s, a 22-item case in 29 s, both inside the clock.
45	**Every chunk submits.** Last write wins and only the state at close is scored, so an
46	intermediate row still at its 0/0 placeholder costs nothing once a later chunk overwrites it,
47	while a board that is never empty survives a crash, a hang or a misjudged clock. 0/0 is also
48	the right blind guess: `b=0` wrongly rejects fair charges at `0.5a` extra each, where `b=∞`
49	would accept fraud up to the cap `c ≥ 4t`. If it fails, nothing is submitted and the exit
50	code is 1 — fall back to `./submit.sh NN 1:A:B ...` by hand.
51	
52	The old **fast** safety pass (a second, smaller model submitted the moment it landed, never
53	aggregated) is off by default and available behind `--fast`. It was insurance from when the
54	full pass ran on `gpt-5.6-sol` at 7–35 s; on terra the single pass lands in 2–7 s, so the
55	second call bought a duplicate answer rather than safety.
56	
57	## How the input is structured
58	
59	The model sees one object, built by `extract.py`:
60	
61	```json
62	{
63	  "game_id": 0,
64	  "policy":      "BICYCLE THEFT INSURANCE ... (full text, never truncated)",
65	  "description": "Client came back from work ... the bike was worth 420 Euros.",
66	  "invoice_text": "full text of invoices.pdf",
67	  "invoice_meta": {"trade": "Bikeshop", "vendor": "Bikey Bike Ltd", "date": "6 Jan 2026"},
68	  "items": [{"index": 1, "description": "New Bike", "quantity": 1, "unit": "unit"}],
69	  "images": [{"name": "...", "media_type": "image/png"}]
70	}
71	```
72	
73	**Case photos are skipped.** `*.png/*.jpg` in the case folder are listed by name in the case
74	dict but never read or attached to the model call: the coverage and pricing decisions come from
75	the policy, the description and the invoice, and image upload costs time inside the 60 s window.
76	
77	**Policy and description are passed verbatim; the model does the reading.** The work —
78	"is a new bike covered under clause 4 given clause 3 and the description says it was
79	locked to a lamp post?" — is cross-referencing natural language, which is what the model
80	is for. The description also carries price signal ("worth 420 Euros") that the model must
81	see next to the invoice.
82	
83	**Nothing is truncated.** Policies run 40–65 KB — under 20k tokens, a rounding error
84	against the context window — and cutting one drops the tail, which is where the exclusions
85	and caps live.
86	
87	They *are* long enough to bury the decisive clauses, so `c2f/policy.py` runs a
88	pre-extraction pass on every game: one call to the same model (`gpt-5.6-terra`, override `C2F_DIGEST_MODEL`) reads policy.txt and returns the parts that
89	bind — insured event, conditions, limits, deductibles, exclusions, obligations — rendered
90	into a `<policy_digest>` block placed *in front of* the verbatim text. It is a reading aid,
91	never a replacement: the full policy is still in the prompt and the prompt says so.
92	
93	Best-effort and bounded. `run.py` starts it in parallel with the **fast** pass (which must
94	never wait — it is the safety submission) and gives the **full** passes `DIGEST_WAIT_S = 10`
95	to pick it up; on timeout or API failure they go with the verbatim policy alone, which is
96	complete. `policy.build()` returns rather than mutates so the main thread owns the assign
97	and cannot race a prompt already being built. `backtest.py` attaches it too, so a replay
98	builds the same prompt as a live run.
99	
100	The invoice is parsed deterministically (`parse_items`: `POS | DESCRIPTION | AMOUNT | UNIT`,
101	wrapped descriptions handled) *and* sent as raw text. The model's item indices are
102	validated against the parse when it succeeded; missing indices are logged and priced as
103	unknown.
104	
105	Prompt layout (`llm.build_user_message`):
106	
107	```
108	<market_history> ... </market_history>   (c2f/history.py: t brackets the market actually accepted
109	                                        in past rounds, by category and by repeated label; omitted
110	                                        if there are no truth files)
111	<policy_digest> ... </policy_digest>   (limits/exclusions pulled out; omitted if that call failed)
112	<policy> ... </policy>
113	<damage_description> ... </damage_description>
114	<invoice trade="Bikeshop" vendor="Bikey Bike Ltd"> raw pdf text </invoice>
115	<parsed_line_items> 1 | New Bike | 1 unit </parsed_line_items>
116	```
117	
118	The system prompt (`llm.SYSTEM`) asks, per item: covered? related? fair **gross total**
119	(qty × unit price, incl. 19 % VAT) as low / mid / high; 0 if not covered, with the
120	would-be price in `t_if_covered`; cite the clause; return JSON only.
121	
122	## Pricing rule (`price.py`)
123	
124	Secret fair value `t` per item. Payoffs: charging `a ≤ t` is always paid; `a > t` is paid
125	only by opponents whose limit `b' ≥ a`. Accepting a fair charge costs 1×, wrongly
126	rejecting costs 1.5×, accepting fraud costs 1× (capped).
127	
128	Belief on `t`: lognormal with median `t_mid × bias` and log-sd `max(σ, model spread)`.
129	`bias`, `σ` (and the market's acceptance of over-charges `p0`, `k`) are learned by
130	`c2f.calibrate` from the `[t_lo, t_hi)` bounds `c2f.truth` recovers after every game
131	(`runs/calibration.json`, read at pricing time; defaults `bias 1, σ 0.4, p0 0.35, k 2`).
132	
133	- **b (acceptance limit)** = 1/3-quantile of the belief.
134	  Accept iff `P(t ≥ a') > 2/3`, from the 1.5× vs 1× asymmetry.
135	- **a (charge)** maximises `mean − 0.75·sd` of the per-opponent payout: `a` if `a ≤ t`, else
136	  `a × p0 × (a/t)^−k` (the fraction of reviewers still accepting an over-charge). A fair
137	  charge is paid by all 16 opponents, a fraudulent one by ~a third → the optimum sits
138	  ~0.5–0.7× the median, lower the less sure we are (the sd term; pure expectation would
139	  chase the upper tail).
140	- **Not covered / not related**: `b = 0`; `a = 0.6 × t_if_covered` (no downside under the
141	  rules: rejected fraud costs the issuer nothing).
142	
143	**No votes.** An earlier version ran the fast pass plus three full-model votes and aggregated
144	them into an ensemble. Comparing fast against full over six logged games
145	(`runs/game_{01,03,04,06,07,08}.json`, scored on the `runs/truth_game_*.json` brackets):
146	the two agreed on 70 of 82 coverage calls, and of the 12 disagreements 4 favoured fast,
147	4 favoured full and 4 were undecidable — a coin flip. On price the full pass *was* clearly
148	better (median |log error| 0.23 vs 0.41 over the 46 items both called covered), so the full
149	pass alone decides the numbers and the fast one is kept only as the fallback submission.
150	
151	Constants at the top of `price.py`: `RISK_AVERSION`, `UNCOVERED_CHARGE`, `B_QUANTILE`.
152	
153	## How far off are t, a and b? (`c2f/deviation.py`)
154	
155	```
156	make deviation                                     # the boards we actually submitted
157	make deviation REPRICE=1 G=14-24                   # stored estimates, priced by today's constants
158	make deviation SWEEP=B_QUANTILE=0.27,0.3333,0.42   # one line per candidate value
159	```
160	
161	`c2f.calibrate` fits the bias and sigma; `c2f.accuracy` says which category is wrong. Neither
162	says how far the three numbers we ship land from the truth, which is what pricing is trying to
163	minimise. This does, on one scale for all three: with `t` known the best charge is `a = t`
164	(anything under is paid by all 16, anything over by only `p0 (a/t)^-k` of them, worth less
165	than `t` everywhere below the `4t` cap) and the best limit is `b = t` (accept iff the charge is
166	fair). So all three targets are the same number and the distances are comparable.
167	
168	Truth is interval-censored, so the distance is too: the gap to `[t_lo, t_hi)`, **0 while the
169	value sits inside the bracket**. Nothing is invented about where inside it `t` sits.
170	
171	The report shows that gap **in euros** — how far the value would have to move to reach the
172	nearest proven bound, summed over the group (`t EUR`, `a EUR`, `b EUR`), with the under/over
173	item counts beside it (`t u/o`) because a net figure hides both directions. The same gap in
174	log units is kept for the `objective` scalar and the `--sweep` table: it is scale-free, and
175	being 50 EUR off on a 60 EUR item is a different mistake from 50 EUR off on 6,000.
176	
177	The regret column needs no assumption at all: `truth_game_NN.json` lists every charge the field
178	issued, and the rules price our mistakes on them exactly — `b` under a charge proven fair costs
179	`0.5c`, `b` over one proven fraudulent costs `min(c, 4t)`, `a` at or under the proven floor
180	leaves `(t_lo - a) x 16` on the table. **That total, not the log distance, is the number to
181	minimise**: distance is symmetric and the payoffs are not, which is why the `b` sweep keeps
182	improving the distance well past the point where refused-fraud money starts costing more than
183	it saves. A sweep winner is a *candidate* — gate it on money the way `c2f.autotune` does (total
184	plus a majority of games) before moving a constant.
185	
186	Per-item rows land in `runs/deviation.json`.
187	
188	## Configuration (`.env`)
189	
190	| Var | Meaning |
191	|---|---|
192	| `TEAM_API_KEY` | QuantCo team key (required) |
193	| `OPENAI_API_KEY` | required — OpenAI is the only provider `c2f/llm.py` and `c2f/policy.py` support |
194	| `C2F_MODEL` | full-pass model (default `gpt-5.6-terra`) |
195	| `C2F_FAST_MODEL` | fast-pass model (default `gpt-5.6-terra`) |
196	| `C2F_DIGEST_MODEL` | policy-digest model (default `gpt-5.6-terra`) |
197	| `C2F_REASONING` | OpenAI `reasoning_effort` for the pass (default `medium`; gpt-5.6 floor is `none`, not `minimal`) |
198	| `C2F_REASONING_FAST` | effort for the optional `--fast` pass (default `none`) |
199	| `C2F_CHUNK_ITEMS` | items per parallel call (default 10) |
200	| `C2F_MAX_CHUNKS` | cap on parallel calls (default 8) |
201	
202	Every one of these is written out in `.env` with the code default made explicit; delete a line
203	and the default in `c2f/` applies.
204	
205	## Logs
206	
207	`runs/game_NN.json`: the case dict, both model outputs with timings,
208	the priced rows, every submission with the server response. This is the material for the
209	strategy write-up.
210	
211	## Backtest (gate for algorithm changes)
212	
213	`c2f/backtest.py` replays the current strategy on past decrypted cases and scores it against
214	the real opponents of that round using the public leaderboard (their charges, their implied
215	accept limits, the inferred `t` bounds). Output: actual vs replayed net and rank per game,
216	pessimistic and optimistic where outcomes are open, `runs/backtest/summary.json`.
217	The verdict — a positive expected net in a majority of games plus a positive total; money is the
218	only gate, rank is reported (top-3 = `RANK_TARGET`) but never fails a run — is always over the
219	**last 10** old games (`WINDOW`) = the 10 most recent completed
220	games with a decrypted case; `make backtest G=...` replays only those games and re-scores the rest
221	from their stored replays, and an old game with no stored replay counts as not won and is listed
222	as `missing`. Running it is a judgement call, not a gate — a pre-commit hook used to enforce it
223	and was removed as too much friction. See `c2f/README.md`.
224	
225	## Not built (deliberately)
226	
227	Scheduler, leaderboard feedback loop, dashboard, database. Manual `make N` per game.

1	"""Turn the model's per-item estimate into (a, b). Pure math, no I/O except the calibration file.
2	
3	a = charge price (what we bill every other team)
4	b = acceptance limit (max we pay when billed the same item)
5	
6	Belief on the fair value t: lognormal, median = t_mid * bias, sigma = max(calibrated sigma,
7	the model's own spread). `bias` and `sigma` are learned by c2f.calibrate from the t bounds
8	c2f.truth recovers after each game (runs/calibration.json); defaults apply until then.
9	
10	- a maximises risk-adjusted revenue, mean - RISK_AVERSION * sd per opponent. A fair charge
11	  (a <= t) is paid by every opponent; a fraudulent one only by the reviewers whose limit is
12	  still above it, a fraction that decays with how far over t it is: p_accept(a/t) = p0 *
13	  (a/t)^-k (also learned from the market). The sd term matters: pure expectation chases the
14	  belief's upper tail and charges MORE the less sure we are; with it, the charge moves from
15	  ~0.7x the median (sigma 0.2) to ~0.5x (sigma 0.8) - crossing t loses ~all the revenue.
16	- b = 1/3-quantile of the belief. Accepting a fair charge costs 1x, wrongly rejecting 1.5x,
17	  accepting fraud 1x -> accept iff P(t >= a') > 2/3.
18	- not covered / not related: b = 0, a = UNCOVERED_CHARGE * bias * t_if_covered (0 if unknown):
19	  a rejected fraudulent charge costs the issuer nothing, so this is free upside. The same
20	  bucket `bias` the covered path applies to t_mid applies here: t_if_covered comes out of the
21	  same call with the same systematic underestimate, so correcting one and not the other was
22	  an inconsistency, not a choice.
23	
24	`other`: a second, independent estimate for the same item (the fast pass, when pricing the
25	full pass). It is a cheap disagreement check, not a vote:
26	- coverage split (one says covered, the other doesn't): neither call clears the confidence a
27	  payout needs, so price as uncertain the same way as "not covered" - b = 0.
28	- both say covered but t_mid lands far apart (>= DISAGREEMENT_RATIO): use the lower, better-
29	  supported mid instead of blindly trusting the full pass, and widen the belief by the gap
30	  between them - this pulls both a and b down, b faster since it already sits below the median.
31	"""
32	
33	from __future__ import annotations
34	
35	import json
36	import math
37	from dataclasses import dataclass, field
38	from pathlib import Path
39	from statistics import NormalDist
40	
41	UNCOVERED_CHARGE = 0.9  # fraction of the would-be price we charge on uncovered items,
42	# multiplied by the same bucket bias the covered path uses (1.48 global today, so ~1.34x
43	# t_if_covered).
44	# Raised from 0.6: over 19 labelled games (c2f.accuracy) 31 of the 101 items we zeroed were
45	# proven covered by the market, against only 5 of 136 priced items proven worthless. Wrongly
46	# rejected fraud costs the issuer nothing, so the only cost of charging near the full
47	# would-be price on an uncovered item is zero - and the upside is the third of them we
48	# excluded by mistake.
49	#
50	# Splitting the branch over games 18-26 (c2f.deviation): the 8 items the market agreed were
51	# worthless cost and earn nothing at ANY multiplier, so all of the money is the 13 items we
52	# zeroed that the market proved had value (game 20 item 1 alone is 61% of the regret).
53	# Expected revenue on those rises to a peak at ~1.5-1.6x t_if_covered and falls off a cliff
54	# past 1.8x as the large items cross the CAP_MULT ceiling; the ranking holds under a
55	# pessimistic acceptance curve (p0 .35, k 2), so it is not the k<1 rail. Taking the bias
56	# rather than the fitted peak keeps the value tracking the market as c2f.calibrate refits.
57	B_QUANTILE = 0.3333  # c2f.autotune over games 1-23: +4,271 vs 0.27, better in 13 games, worse in 4 - the
58	# only candidate the gate accepted, and it takes the last-10 backtest from 5/10 profitable to passing.
59	# (0.27 was itself +1,801 over 0.20 across games 1-17.) The game 6 electronics guard still holds at this
60	# value once that test is pointed at the one-pass path we actually run: b=902 against a real t under 900.
61	# The earlier walk down from 0.27 to 0.18 (games 6-10) overshot slightly: the market's t now runs
62	# ABOVE our t_mid (calibrated bias 1.19), so refused fair charges cost more than they used to.
63	RISK_AVERSION = 0.55  # charge maximises mean - RISK_AVERSION * sd of the per-opponent payout.
64	# c2f.autotune over games 1-14: +8,906 vs 0.585, better in 9 games and worse in 2. It matches the
65	# post-mortem (UNDERCHARGE 78k, UNDER_ESTIMATE 97k - we were too timid on both sides) and the
66	# calibrated bias of 1.19, which says the market's t sits ABOVE our t_mid.
67	#
68	# 0.30-0.50 scored better still (+10,415) and the backtest passed, but all three break the rail
69	# this term exists for: below ~0.52 the charge stops FALLING as the belief widens, because a
70	# slowly-decaying acceptance curve (fitted k = 0.6) makes overcharging look profitable right up to
71	# the CAP_MULT ceiling. That is true of today's lenient field and false the moment it tightens, and
72	# crossing t costs ~all the revenue on that line. 0.55 buys 86% of the gain and keeps the rail.
73	# 0.85 was rejected by the backtest gate rather than the total: only 2/5 recent games profitable.
74	CAP_MULT = 4.0  # an accepted over-charge pays at most min(a, c) with c >= 4t (the rules' cap)
75	MODEL_SPREAD_Z = 1.2816  # the model's t_low..t_high is read as an 80 % interval
76	N_GRID = 200
77	
78	DISAGREEMENT_RATIO = 1.6  # two passes this far apart on t_mid: use the lower one, don't average
79	CAP_UNCERTAIN_B_SHRINK = 0.7  # extra caution on b when a referenced policy cap's value is unknown
80	
81	class InvalidEstimateError(ValueError):
82	    """A covered+related item reached pricing with t_low=t_mid=t_high<=0 - the SYSTEM
83	    contract (c2f.llm.SYSTEM) requires a positive t_mid for such items. This must be
84	    repaired or replaced upstream (c2f.validate + the targeted repair pass in c2f.run),
85	    never priced here as if the item were uncovered - see the Game 10 item 3 postmortem."""
86	
87	    def __init__(self, index: object, message: str):
88	        self.index = index
89	        super().__init__(message)
90	
91	
92	BIAS_RANGE = (0.4, 2.5)  # expanded to allow more aggressive category-specific correction
93	SIGMA_RANGE = (0.15, 1.0)
94	P0_RANGE = (0.02, 0.8)
95	K_RANGE = (0.0, 6.0)
96	#: description keyword -> bucket. First match wins, so order matters: the specific
97	#: trades come before the generic "labour" and "material" catch-alls.
98	BUCKETS: list[tuple[str, tuple[str, ...]]] = [
99	    ("ancillary/call-out", ("vehicle", "travel", "call-out", "callout", "shipping", "delivery",
100	                            "disposal", "admin", "postage", "mileage")),
101	    ("diagnostic/inspect", ("diagnos", "inspect", "assess", "report", "survey", "measurement",
102	                            "moisture", "leak detection", "detection")),
103	    ("drying/remediation", ("drying", "dehumid", "dryer", "fan", "vacuum", "extract",
104	                            "stabilis", "stabiliz")),
105	    ("electronics", ("tv", "television", "speaker", "laptop", "computer", "monitor", "console",
106	                     "camera", "phone", "audio", "electronic", "appliance")),
107	    ("valuables", ("watch", "jewel", "ring", "gold", "bicycle", "bike", "sunglasses", "designer")),
108	    ("labour", ("hour", "hrs", "worker", "technician", "helper", "labour", "labor", "fitter")),
109	    ("restoration/repair", ("restor", "repair", "renovat", "conservat", "paint", "tiling",
110	                            "plaster", "skirting", "floor", "wall")),
111	    ("material", ("material", "parts", "supply", "consumable")),
112	]
113	
114	
115	def bucket_of(description: str) -> str:
116	    d = (description or "").lower()
117	    for name, keys in BUCKETS:
118	        if any(k in d for k in keys):
119	            return name
120	    return "other"
121	
122	
123	CALIBRATION_PATH = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent / "runs" / "calibration.json"
124	
125	_N = NormalDist()
126	
127	
128	@dataclass(frozen=True)
129	class Calibration:
130	    bias: float = 1.0  # true t / model t_mid, median
131	    sigma: float = 0.4  # log-sd of true t around bias * t_mid
132	    p0: float = 0.35  # fraction of reviewers accepting a charge just over t
133	    k: float = 2.0  # acceptance decays as (a/t)^-k beyond t
134	    #: bucket -> bias, where the labels support it. One global bias averages over
135	    #: categories whose errors point in OPPOSITE directions: measured over games 12-17
136	    #: we under-price material (median t_lo/t_mid 2.15) and labour (1.52) while
137	    #: over-pricing drying/remediation (0.74) and restoration/repair (0.72), so a single
138	    #: multiplier of 1.37 makes those last two worse. c2f.calibrate fits each bucket and
139	    #: shrinks it toward the global one, so a thin bucket cannot swing far on 5 labels.
140	    bias_by_bucket: dict[str, float] = field(default_factory=dict)
141	
142	    def bias_for(self, description: str | None) -> float:
143	        """Bucket bias when we have one, else the global. Never guesses from a blank."""
144	        if not description:
145	            return self.bias
146	        return self.bias_by_bucket.get(bucket_of(description), self.bias)
147	
148	
149	DEFAULT_CALIBRATION = Calibration()
150	
151	
152	def _clamp(v: float, rng: tuple[float, float]) -> float:
153	    return min(rng[1], max(rng[0], v))
154	
155	
156	def calibration() -> Calibration:
157	    """Learned calibration (runs/calibration.json), clamped; the default if missing or broken."""
158	    try:
159	        d = json.loads(CALIBRATION_PATH.read_text())
160	        vals = {k: float(d[k]) for k in ("bias", "sigma", "p0", "k")}
161	    except (OSError, ValueError, KeyError, TypeError):
162	        return DEFAULT_CALIBRATION
163	    if not all(math.isfinite(v) for v in vals.values()):
164	        return DEFAULT_CALIBRATION
165	    raw = d.get("bias_by_bucket") or {}
166	    buckets = {}
167	    if isinstance(raw, dict):
168	        for name, v in raw.items():
169	            try:
170	                fv = float(v)
171	            except (TypeError, ValueError):
172	                continue
173	            if math.isfinite(fv):
174	                buckets[str(name)] = _clamp(fv, BIAS_RANGE)
175	    return Calibration(
176	        bias=_clamp(vals["bias"], BIAS_RANGE),
177	        sigma=_clamp(vals["sigma"], SIGMA_RANGE),
178	        p0=_clamp(vals["p0"], P0_RANGE),
179	        k=_clamp(vals["k"], K_RANGE),
180	        bias_by_bucket=buckets,
181	    )

184	def _num(x: object) -> float:
185	    try:
186	        v = float(x)  # type: ignore[arg-type]
187	    except (TypeError, ValueError):
188	        return 0.0
189	    return v if math.isfinite(v) and v > 0 else 0.0

192	@dataclass(frozen=True)
193	class Belief:
194	    """Lognormal belief on t: ln t ~ N(mu, sigma^2)."""
195	
196	    mu: float
197	    sigma: float
198	
199	    @property
200	    def median(self) -> float:
201	        return math.exp(self.mu)
202	
203	    def quantile(self, q: float) -> float:
204	        return math.exp(self.mu + self.sigma * _N.inv_cdf(q))
205	
206	    @classmethod
207	    def from_estimate(cls, est: dict, cal: Calibration) -> "Belief":
208	        lo, mid, hi = sorted(_num(est.get(k)) for k in ("t_low", "t_mid", "t_high"))
209	        model_sigma = (math.log(hi) - math.log(lo)) / (2 * MODEL_SPREAD_Z) if lo > 0 and hi > lo else 0.0
210	        return cls(mu=math.log(mid * cal.bias_for(est.get("_description"))), sigma=_clamp(max(cal.sigma, model_sigma), SIGMA_RANGE))
211	
212	
213	def accept_limit(belief: Belief) -> float:
214	    return belief.quantile(B_QUANTILE)

217	def best_charge(belief: Belief, cal: Calibration, n_grid: int = N_GRID, risk_aversion: float | None = None) -> float:
218	    """Charge maximising mean - risk_aversion * sd of the per-opponent payout, over the belief's quantiles.
219	
220	    Never above the median (a charge more likely fraud than fair is not a price, it is a bet), and an
221	    accepted over-charge pays at most CAP_MULT * t - without that cap a slowly decaying acceptance
222	    curve (k < 1) would reward charging the moon."""
223	    if risk_aversion is None:
224	        risk_aversion = RISK_AVERSION
225	    ts = [belief.quantile((j + 0.5) / n_grid) for j in range(n_grid)]
226	    best_a, best_v = 0.0, -math.inf
227	    for a in ts:
228	        if a > belief.median:
229	            break
230	        pays = [a if a <= t else min(a, CAP_MULT * t) * cal.p0 * (t / a) ** cal.k for t in ts]
231	        mean = sum(pays) / n_grid
232	        sd = math.sqrt(sum((x - mean) ** 2 for x in pays) / n_grid)
233	        v = mean - risk_aversion * sd
234	        if v > best_v:
235	            best_a, best_v = a, v
236	    return best_a

239	def _has_bundle_keywords(description: str | None) -> bool:
240	    """Detect likely bundled items with multiple distinct components."""
241	    if not description:
242	        return False
243	    d = (description or "").lower()
244	    # Common bundling patterns: multiple appliances, multiple plumbing components, etc.
245	    bundle_indicators = [
246	        ("boiler", "tank", "flue", "pipework", "heater", "valve"),
247	        ("repair", "replacement", "adjustment"),
248	    ]
249	    # Check if description mentions structural terms suggesting bundled work
250	    component_keywords = [
251	        "boiler", "flue", "tank", "pipework", "heater", "valve", "radiator",
252	        "pipe", "fitting", "gasket", "thermostat", "pump",
253	        "installation", "removal", "adjustment", "alignment",
254	    ]
255	    keyword_count = sum(1 for kw in component_keywords if kw in d)
256	    return keyword_count >= 2

259	def _validate_bundle_coverage(est: dict) -> bool:
260	    """For bundled items marked covered, verify component coverage is explicit.
261	
262	    If an item description mentions multiple components/operations and is marked
263	    covered, the reason/clause should explicitly mention that each component is
264	    covered. If coverage is unclear for any component, return False to mark the
265	    entire bundle as uncovered (never invent allocations).
266	    """
267	    if not est.get("covered"):
268	        return True  # Not covered, no need to validate bundle
269	
270	    description = est.get("_description", "") or est.get("description", "")
271	    if not _has_bundle_keywords(description):
272	        return True  # Not a bundle, normal coverage applies
273	
274	    reason = (est.get("reason") or "").lower()
275	    clause = (est.get("clause") or "").lower()
276	    evidence_text = (reason + " " + clause).lower()
277	
278	    # Check for negative indicators: if the reason mentions uncertainty or exclusions
279	    # for any component, the entire bundle is uncovered
280	    uncertainty_phrases = [
281	        "uncertain", "unclear", "not established", "not clear", "potentially",
282	        "may be excluded", "may not be", "questionable", "disputed",
283	    ]
284	    for phrase in uncertainty_phrases:
285	        if phrase in evidence_text:
286	            return False
287	
288	    # For a bundled replacement, all key components must be explicitly mentioned
289	    # as covered. Extract components from description and verify coverage mention.
290	    component_keywords = {
291	        "boiler": ("boiler", "heating", "furnace"),
292	        "flue": ("flue", "chimney", "vent"),
293	        "tank": ("tank", "vessel", "cylinder", "storage"),
294	        "pipework": ("pipe", "pipework", "plumbing", "fitting"),
295	        "installation": ("install", "fit", "fit", "assemble"),
296	        "removal": ("remov", "strip", "dismantle"),
297	        "adjustment": ("adjust", "align", "balance"),
298	    }
299	
300	    description_lower = description.lower()
301	    mentioned_components = []
302	    for comp_name, keywords in component_keywords.items():
303	        if any(kw in description_lower for kw in keywords):
304	            mentioned_components.append(comp_name)
305	
306	    # If multiple components are mentioned, all must be explicitly covered in evidence
307	    if len(mentioned_components) >= 2:
308	        # Check that the reason/clause mentions the key operation being covered
309	        covered_phrases = [
310	            "covered", "indemnifi", "reimburse", "claim", "payable", "insured",
311	        ]
312	        has_coverage_language = any(phrase in evidence_text for phrase in covered_phrases)
313	        if not has_coverage_language:
314	            return False
315	
316	    return True
317

319	def price_item(est: dict, cal: Calibration | None = None, other: dict | None = None) -> tuple[float, float]:
320	    """Return (a, b) as gross totals, both finite and >= 0.
321	
322	    `other`, if given, is a second independent estimate for the same item - see module
323	    docstring for how a coverage split or a wide t_mid gap between the two is handled."""
324	    cal = cal or calibration()
325	    covered = bool(est.get("covered", False)) and bool(est.get("related", True))
326	
327	    # Gate: validate bundle coverage BEFORE any pricing. If bundle coverage is not
328	    # established (evidence doesn't cover all components), treat as truly uncovered.
329	    bundle_coverage_valid = True
330	    if covered:
331	        bundle_coverage_valid = _validate_bundle_coverage(est)
332	        if not bundle_coverage_valid:
333	            covered = False
334	
335	    mid = sorted(_num(est.get(k)) for k in ("t_low", "t_mid", "t_high"))[1]
336	
337	    other_covered = other_mid = None
338	    other_bundle_valid = True
339	    if other is not None:
340	        other_covered = bool(other.get("covered", False)) and bool(other.get("related", True))
341	        if other_covered:
342	            other_bundle_valid = _validate_bundle_coverage(other)
343	            if not other_bundle_valid:
344	                other_covered = False
345	        other_mid = sorted(_num(other.get(k)) for k in ("t_low", "t_mid", "t_high"))[1]
346	
347	    if other_covered is not None and other_covered != covered:
348	        # split coverage call: not confident enough either way to pay out
349	        guess = _num(est.get("t_if_covered")) or mid or other_mid or _num(other.get("t_if_covered"))
350	        return round(UNCOVERED_CHARGE * guess, 2), 0.0
351	
352	    if not covered:
353	        # For items failing bundle validation, return a=0, b=0 to enforce strict
354	        # coverage. For normal uncovered items, apply UNCOVERED_CHARGE.
355	        if bundle_coverage_valid == False and bool(est.get("covered", False)):
356	            # Model said covered but validation rejected due to bundle components
357	            return 0.0, 0.0
358	        guess = _num(est.get("t_if_covered")) or mid
359	        return round(UNCOVERED_CHARGE * guess, 2), 0.0
360	
361	    if mid <= 0:
362	        raise InvalidEstimateError(
363	            est.get("index"),
364	            f"item {est.get('index')}: covered and related but t_low=t_mid=t_high<=0 - "
365	            "invalid state, must be repaired before pricing, not priced as uncovered",
366	        )
367	
368	    est_for_belief, disagreement_sigma = est, 0.0
369	    if other_mid and mid > 0 and max(mid, other_mid) / min(mid, other_mid) >= DISAGREEMENT_RATIO:
370	        est_for_belief = {**est, "t_mid": min(mid, other_mid)}
371	        disagreement_sigma = (math.log(max(mid, other_mid)) - math.log(min(mid, other_mid))) / (2 * MODEL_SPREAD_Z)
372	
373	    belief = Belief.from_estimate(est_for_belief, cal)
374	    if disagreement_sigma:
375	        belief = Belief(mu=belief.mu, sigma=_clamp(max(belief.sigma, disagreement_sigma), SIGMA_RANGE))
376	
377	    a = best_charge(belief, cal)
378	    b = accept_limit(belief)
379	    if bool(est.get("cap_uncertain")):
380	        b *= CAP_UNCERTAIN_B_SHRINK
381	    return round(a, 2), round(b, 2)
382	
383	
384	def price_all(estimates: list[dict], other_output: dict | None = None) -> list[dict]:
385	    """`other_output`, if given, is a second model's raw {items: [...]} output for the same
386	    case - used as the disagreement check in price_item (see module docstring)."""
387	    cal = calibration()
388	    other_by_idx: dict[int, dict] = {}
389	    for it in (other_output or {}).get("items", []):
390	        try:
391	            other_by_idx[int(it["index"])] = it
392	        except (KeyError, TypeError, ValueError):
393	            continue
394	    out = []
395	    for est in estimates:
396	        idx = int(est["index"])
397	        a, b = price_item(est, cal, other=other_by_idx.get(idx))
398	        out.append({"index": idx, "charge_price": a, "acceptance_limit": b})
399	    return out

17	SYSTEM = """You are a senior insurance claims expert working in Germany. You assess invoices
18	submitted after an insured event. For EVERY line item on the invoice you decide:
19	
20	1. covered  - Is this type of cost insured under the policy text? Check the insured
21	              event, conditions of cover, amount of indemnity and exclusions. When in doubt,
22	              prefer COVERED unless there is explicit evidence the item is excluded. Only answer
23	              NOT covered when:
24	              - the policy explicitly names the item/category in an exclusions clause, OR
25	              - the cost type is clearly unrelated to insured events (e.g. upgrades, preventive
26	                maintenance, unrelated damage, cosmetic-only repairs), OR
27	              - the item predates the insured event or is for scheduled maintenance.
28	              Ambiguity about quantity, condition, or price does NOT make an item uncovered.
29	              Uncertainty about the exact clause that covers it is NOT a reason to say NOT covered.
30	2. related  - Does this line item belong to the reported damage described? An item
31	              that is unrelated to the event (or clearly excessive in kind, e.g. an
32	              upgrade instead of a repair) is not related. When unsure if an item relates to
33	              the described damage, prefer RELATED unless there is clear evidence it does not.
34	3. fair gross total - the TOTAL price for the whole line (quantity x unit price,
35	              INCLUDING 19% German VAT, in EUR) that a careful claims expert would
36	              still accept as reasonable. Break this down into:
37	                - What is the unit of the cost? (per hour, per item, per m², flat call-out, project price)
38	                - How many units are involved? (from the quantity field, or reason from the description)
39	                - What is a plausible market unit price in Germany in 2026?
40	                - Multiply to get the gross total including VAT.
41	              Then give three numbers:
42	                t_low  : a price almost certainly acceptable (use cheapest reasonable item/rate)
43	                t_mid  : your best single estimate of the maximum acceptable price
44	                t_high : a price that is probably already too expensive
45	              Use market prices in Germany in 2026 for a standard / mid-range
46	              replacement or a typical tradesman rate - NOT premium brands, NOT
47	              worst-case. For bundled services (inspection, diagnosis, call-out), price only the
48	              QUANTITY needed to address the damage, never the full invoice quantity unless
49	              explicitly justified. Claims experts are frugal: when unsure, go lower. Use any
50	              value hints in the damage description (stated worth, age, make, size). Respect policy limits
51	              (sum insured, market value, caps, deductibles) - t must not exceed them.
52	
53	              BUT the description's own characterisation of the item binds: if it
54	              calls something "expensive", "designer", "luxury", "premium",
55	              "high-end" or names a premium brand, the fair value is
56	              that tier's like-for-like replacement (an "expensive watch" is a
57	              several-thousand-euro watch, not a standard one). Frugal means no
58	              invented upgrades, not ignoring stated value.
59	
60	              NEVER INVENT SPECIFICS. If the invoice/description does not state a brand,
61	              model, screen size, wattage, channel count or other premium feature, do not
62	              assume one - price the CHEAPEST reasonable standard replacement that matches
63	              only what is actually stated, not a mid-range guess dressed up with invented
64	              detail. When the evidence for a number is weak (no stated size/spec/age/price),
65	              make t_low MUCH more conservative than t_mid - at least 2-3x lower, closer to the
66	              cheapest plausible bottom-of-market item. A low t_low costs nothing (it only raises b)
67	              while an inflated one risks accepting fraud. The asymmetry matters: being 2x too low on
68	              t_low costs zero; being 2x too high costs real money when opponents exploit it.
69	
70	              Bundled diagnostic, inspection, call-out or service charges: price only the
71	              ONE necessary visit/report, never the full billed quantity, unless the
72	              invoice or description gives a specific reason for more than one.
73	
74	   COMMON FAILURE MODES TO AVOID:
75	   - Confusing repair/restoration cost with replacement cost: repair is always cheaper.
76	   - Pricing the whole project when the invoice is for one small component within it.
77	   - Over-interpreting "labour" costs: a 2-hour job should be ~€50-150, not €2,000.
78	   - Misunderstanding quantity: if quantity=1 but description says "per hour" or "per m²",
79	     check if the invoice text specifies the actual hours/area - the quantity field is often generic.
80	   - Treating "diagnostic/inspection" as premium services: they are cost-effective services,
81	     typically €50-300, not €5,000 unless it is a major specialist survey.
82	   - Assuming "expensive" items are luxury goods: the invoice context (e.g. "replaced the damaged
83	     watch") means fair market replacement, not premium resale value.
84	
85	   If the policy text refers to a cap, sub-limit or schedule value for this item's category
86	   but does not state the number (e.g. "as per Appendix B" with no figure given), set
87	   "cap_uncertain": true and keep your estimate conservative - do not guess the cap's value.
88	   Otherwise omit cap_uncertain or set it false.
89	
90	   If the item is not covered OR not related, set t_low = t_mid = t_high = 0 and put
91	   your estimate of what the item WOULD cost if it were payable into t_if_covered.

126	def build_user_message(case: dict, only: list[int] | None = None, sweep: bool = False) -> str:
127	    # No <parsed_line_items> block: the invoice is not line-parsed (see c2f.extract). The
128	    # model reads the full pdf text and decides for itself what the line items are.
129	    meta = case.get("invoice_meta") or {}
130	    meta_txt = " ".join(f'{k}="{v}"' for k, v in meta.items())
131	    # A fast model's extract of the clauses that bind (c2f.policy). Absent if that call failed:
132	    # it is a reading aid in front of the verbatim policy below, never a replacement for it.
133	    digest = case.get("policy_digest")
134	    digest_txt = (
135	        f"<policy_digest note=\"limits, deductibles and exclusions pulled out of the policy below; "
136	        f"a reading aid - the full policy text is authoritative\">\n{digest}\n</policy_digest>\n\n"
137	        if digest
138	        else ""
139	    )
140	    return (
141	        # Past rounds' recovered t brackets (c2f.history). Evidence for the size of a number,
142	        # in front of the case so it frames the reading rather than second-guessing it after.
143	        HISTORY
144	        + digest_txt
145	        + f"<policy>\n{case['policy']}\n</policy>\n\n"
146	        f"<damage_description>\n{case['description']}\n</damage_description>\n\n"
147	        f"<invoice {meta_txt}>\n{case['invoice_text']}\n</invoice>\n"
148	        # Chunking keeps the WHOLE policy and invoice in front of the model and narrows only
149	        # the answer. Splitting the context instead would cost the cross-item signal - a
150	        # duplicated line, or labour inconsistent with the parts fitted - which is exactly
151	        # what a single whole-invoice call was for.
152	        + (
153	            "\nPRICE ONLY THESE POS NUMBERS: "
154	            + ", ".join(str(i) for i in only)
155	            + f". Return exactly {len(only)} objects, one per listed POS number"
156	            + (
157	                # One chunk keeps the job of catching what the parser missed. Game 11 had 22
158	                # line items across several invoices, the parser found 11, and the 11 it never
159	                # saw went out at 0/0 - two thirds of that round's loss.
160	                ", PLUS one object for every POS number that appears in the invoice text above"
161	                " but is missing from the parsed list. Do not lose those.\n"
162	                if sweep
163	                else ", and no others. The rest of the invoice is context only.\n"
164	            )
165	            if only
166	            else ""
167	        )
168	        + "\nReturn the JSON now."
169	    )

172	def _parse_json(text: str) -> dict:
173	    text = text.strip()
174	    m = re.search(r"\{.*\}", text, re.S)
175	    if not m:
176	        raise ValueError(f"no JSON in model output: {text[:200]!r}")
177	    return json.loads(m.group(0))

180	def _call_openai(case: dict, model: str, timeout: float, system: str = SYSTEM, fast: bool = False, only: list[int] | None = None, sweep: bool = False) -> str:
181	    from openai import OpenAI

183	    client = OpenAI(api_key=os.environ["OPENAI_API_KEY"], timeout=timeout, max_retries=0)
184	    # Text only: case photos are skipped (case["images"] is names, no bytes). They cost

186	    # policy, the description and the invoice.

188	    kwargs: dict = {}

234	def estimate(case: dict, *, timeout: float = 35.0, model: str | None = None, strict: bool = False,
235	             only: list[int] | None = None, sweep: bool = False) -> tuple[dict, dict]:

247	    # same prompt (12,13,14,16,17,19,20,21,22, scored against runs/truth_game_*.json), terra and
248	    # sol call coverage identically (89% each) and terra prices no worse (median |log t error|
249	    # 0.33 vs 0.39) - at roughly a third of the latency (2.4 s vs 6.8 s on game 22), which inside
250	    # a 60 s clock is the whole ballgame. No measured reason to pay for two.
251	    model = model or os.environ.get("C2F_MODEL") or "gpt-5.6-terra"
252	    raw = _call_openai(case, model, timeout, system, fast=strict, only=only, sweep=sweep)
253	    out = _parse_json(raw)
254	    if "items" not in out or not isinstance(out["items"], list):
255	        raise ValueError("model JSON has no items list")
256	    meta = {"provider": prov, "model": model, "seconds": round(time.time() - t0, 2), "raw": raw}
257	    errors = validate_items(out)
258	    if errors:
259	        meta["validation_errors"] = [str(e) for e in errors]
260	    return out, meta

1	"""Learn how the model's t estimates relate to the truth, and how the market treats over-charges.
2	
3	  pixi run python -m c2f.calibrate        # reads runs/truth_game_*.json, runs/feedback_game_*.json, runs/game_NN.json
4	
5	1. bias, sigma: every item with a proven bound (t_lo > 0 and/or t_hi) and a model estimate t_mid
6	   is an interval on ln(t / t_mid). Fit a normal (bias = exp(mean), sigma) by maximum
7	   interval-censored likelihood - two-sided, so over- and under-estimates both count.
8	2. p0, k: how many reviewers still accept a charge that is over t. From the feedback digests,
9	   for every charge proven fraudulent on an item whose t is bracketed, (a / t*, accept fraction)
10	   with t* the geometric midpoint of the bracket; fit p0 * r^-k by least squares.
11	Writes runs/calibration.json, which c2f.price reads at pricing time.
12	"""
13	
14	from __future__ import annotations
15	
16	import json
17	import math
18	import statistics
19	import sys
20	from statistics import NormalDist
21	
22	from c2f.extract import case_labels
23	from c2f.price import bucket_of, BIAS_RANGE, CALIBRATION_PATH, DEFAULT_CALIBRATION, K_RANGE, P0_RANGE, SIGMA_RANGE
24	from c2f.submit import ROOT
25	
26	MIN_LABELS = 4
27	MIN_ACCEPT_POINTS = 6
28	_N = NormalDist()
29	
30	
31	def estimates(game_id: int) -> dict[int, dict]:
32	    """Per item model estimate used in that game (newest key first; old logs used an ensemble)."""
33	    for name in (f"game_{game_id:02d}.json", f"dry_game_{game_id:02d}.json"):
34	        p = ROOT / "runs" / name
35	        if not p.exists():
36	            continue
37	        rec = json.loads(p.read_text())
38	        out = (
39	            rec.get("estimate")
40	            or rec.get("ensemble")  # runs from when several votes were aggregated
41	            or (rec.get("model_full") or {}).get("output")
42	            or (rec.get("model_full0") or {}).get("output")
43	        )
44	        if out:
45	            items = {int(it["index"]): it for it in out["items"]}
46	            descs = case_labels(rec.get("case", {}))
47	            # NOT setdefault: runs from games 27-29 have "_description": "" already serialised into
48	            # the stored estimate, so setdefault kept the blank and the recovered label never landed.
49	            for i, it in items.items():
50	                if not it.get("_description"):
51	                    it["_description"] = descs.get(i, "")
52	            return items
53	    return {}
54	
55	
56	def labels() -> list[dict]:
57	    rows = []
58	    for p in sorted((ROOT / "runs").glob("truth_game_*.json")):
59	        g = int(p.stem.split("_")[-1])
60	        truth = json.loads(p.read_text())
61	        est = estimates(g)
62	        for i, tv in truth.items():
63	            it = est.get(int(i))
64	            if not it:
65	                continue
66	            lo, hi = float(tv["t_lo"] or 0.0), tv.get("t_hi")
67	            if lo <= 0 and hi is None:
68	                continue
69	            mid = float(it.get("t_mid") or 0)
70	            covered = bool(it.get("covered")) and bool(it.get("related", True)) and mid > 0
71	            rows.append({"game": g, "item": int(i), "t_lo": lo, "t_hi": hi, "t_mid": mid,
72	                         "covered": covered, "bucket": bucket_of(it.get("_description", ""))})
73	    return rows
74	
75	
76	def _loglik(rows: list[dict], mu: float, sigma: float) -> float:
77	    ll = 0.0
78	    for r in rows:
79	        lo = _N.cdf((math.log(r["t_lo"]) - math.log(r["t_mid"]) - mu) / sigma) if r["t_lo"] > 0 else 0.0
80	        hi = _N.cdf((math.log(r["t_hi"]) - math.log(r["t_mid"]) - mu) / sigma) if r["t_hi"] else 1.0
81	        ll += math.log(max(hi - lo, 1e-9))
82	    return ll
83	
84	
85	def fit_bias_sigma(rows: list[dict]) -> tuple[float, float]:
86	    """rows: {t_lo, t_hi (or None), t_mid>0}. Grid MLE of the interval-censored normal on ln(t/t_mid)."""
87	    rows = [r for r in rows if r["t_mid"] > 0 and (r["t_lo"] > 0 or r.get("t_hi"))]
88	    best, best_ll = (0.0, DEFAULT_CALIBRATION.sigma), -math.inf
89	    mus = [math.log(BIAS_RANGE[0]) + i * (math.log(BIAS_RANGE[1]) - math.log(BIAS_RANGE[0])) / 100 for i in range(101)]
90	    sigmas = [SIGMA_RANGE[0] + i * (SIGMA_RANGE[1] - SIGMA_RANGE[0]) / 85 for i in range(86)]
91	    for mu in mus:
92	        for s in sigmas:
93	            ll = _loglik(rows, mu, s)
94	            if ll > best_ll:
95	                best, best_ll = (mu, s), ll
96	    return math.exp(best[0]), best[1]
97	
98	
99	#: Shrinkage weight: a bucket needs this many labels before it moves half way from the
100	#: global bias to its own fit. Keeps a 5-label bucket from swinging the price.
101	BUCKET_PRIOR = 6.0
102	MIN_BUCKET_LABELS = 4
103	
104	
105	def fit_bucket_bias(rows: list[dict], global_bias: float) -> dict[str, float]:
106	    """Per-bucket bias, shrunk toward `global_bias` in log space (James-Stein style).
107	
108	    Fitting each bucket independently on 5-15 labels would just fit noise - that is the
109	    same mistake the accept-limit sweep made when it found an "optimum" driven by one
110	    game. Shrinking means a thin bucket barely moves and a well-evidenced one moves most
111	    of the way.
112	    """
113	    out: dict[str, float] = {}
114	    by: dict[str, list[dict]] = {}
115	    for r in rows:
116	        if r["t_mid"] > 0 and (r["t_lo"] > 0 or r.get("t_hi")):
117	            by.setdefault(r.get("bucket", "other"), []).append(r)
118	    for name, rs in by.items():
119	        if len(rs) < MIN_BUCKET_LABELS:
120	            continue
121	        b, _sigma = fit_bias_sigma(rs)
122	        n = len(rs)
123	        shrunk = math.exp((n * math.log(b) + BUCKET_PRIOR * math.log(global_bias)) / (n + BUCKET_PRIOR))
124	        out[name] = round(shrunk, 3)
125	    return out
126	
127	
128	def acceptance_points() -> list[tuple[float, float]]:
129	    """(a / t*, fraction of reviewers accepting) for charges proven fraudulent on bracketed items."""
130	    pts = []
131	    for p in sorted((ROOT / "runs").glob("truth_game_*.json")):
132	        g = int(p.stem.split("_")[-1])
133	        fp = ROOT / "runs" / f"feedback_game_{g:02d}.json"
134	        if not fp.exists():
135	            continue
136	        truth = json.loads(p.read_text())
137	        fb = json.loads(fp.read_text())
138	        for i, tv in truth.items():
139	            lo, hi = float(tv["t_lo"] or 0.0), tv.get("t_hi")
140	            if lo <= 0 or not hi:
141	                continue
142	            t_star = math.sqrt(lo * hi)
143	            for team in fb["teams"]:
144	                a = fb["issued"].get(team, {}).get(i)
145	                acc = fb["accepted"].get(team, {}).get(i) or []
146	                if not a or a < hi or not acc:
147	                    continue
148	                pts.append((a / t_star, sum(bool(x) for x in acc) / len(acc)))
149	    return pts
150	
151	
152	def fit_acceptance(pts: list[tuple[float, float]]) -> tuple[float, float]:
153	    """Least-squares fit of frac = p0 * r^-k over a grid."""
154	    best, best_err = (DEFAULT_CALIBRATION.p0, DEFAULT_CALIBRATION.k), math.inf
155	    for i in range(79):
156	        p0 = P0_RANGE[0] + i * (P0_RANGE[1] - P0_RANGE[0]) / 78
157	        for j in range(61):
158	            k = K_RANGE[0] + j * (K_RANGE[1] - K_RANGE[0]) / 60
159	            err = sum((f - p0 * r ** -k) ** 2 for r, f in pts)
160	            if err < best_err:
161	                best, best_err = (p0, k), err
162	    return best
163	
164	
165	def main() -> None:
166	    rows = labels()
167	    fit_rows = [r for r in rows if r["covered"] and r["t_lo"] > 0]
168	    missed = [r for r in rows if (not r["covered"] and r["t_lo"] > 0) or (r["covered"] and r["t_lo"] <= 0 and r["t_hi"] and r["t_hi"] < 0.5 * r["t_mid"])]
169	    bias, sigma = DEFAULT_CALIBRATION.bias, DEFAULT_CALIBRATION.sigma
170	    if len(fit_rows) >= MIN_LABELS:
171	        bias, sigma = fit_bias_sigma(fit_rows)
172	    pts = acceptance_points()
173	    p0, k = DEFAULT_CALIBRATION.p0, DEFAULT_CALIBRATION.k
174	    if len(pts) >= MIN_ACCEPT_POINTS:
175	        p0, k = fit_acceptance(pts)
176	    for r in rows:
177	        hi = f"{r['t_hi']:7.0f}" if r["t_hi"] else "    inf"
178	        tag = "ok" if r["covered"] and r["t_lo"] > 0 else ("model said NOT covered, t > 0" if not r["covered"] else "model said covered, t may be 0")
179	        print(f"  game {r['game']:2d} item {r['item']:2d}: t in [{r['t_lo']:7.0f}, {hi})  t_mid {r['t_mid']:7.0f}  {tag}")
180	    print(f"{len(fit_rows)} bracketed covered items -> bias {bias:.2f}, sigma {sigma:.2f}; {len(missed)} coverage misses")
181	    buckets = fit_bucket_bias(fit_rows, bias)
182	    print(f"{len(pts)} over-charge acceptance points -> p0 {p0:.2f}, k {k:.2f}")
183	    if buckets:
184	        spread = f"{min(buckets.values()):.2f}-{max(buckets.values()):.2f}"
185	        print(f"per-category bias ({len(buckets)} buckets, shrunk toward {bias:.2f}, range {spread}):")
186	        for name, b in sorted(buckets.items(), key=lambda kv: -kv[1]):
187	            arrow = "raise" if b > bias else ("lower" if b < bias else "same")
188	            print(f"    {name:<20} {b:>5.2f}  ({arrow} vs global)")
189	    CALIBRATION_PATH.write_text(json.dumps({
190	        "bias": round(bias, 3), "sigma": round(sigma, 3), "p0": round(p0, 3), "k": round(k, 3),
191	        "bias_by_bucket": buckets,
192	        "n_labels": len(fit_rows), "n_coverage_misses": len(missed), "n_accept_points": len(pts),
193	        "labels": [{k2: r[k2] for k2 in ("game", "item", "t_lo", "t_hi", "t_mid")} for r in fit_rows],
194	    }, indent=1))
195	    print(f"saved {CALIBRATION_PATH.relative_to(ROOT)}")
196	
197	
198	if __name__ == "__main__":
199	    sys.exit(main())
200

1	# 🏆 Claim to Fame
2	
3	Hello hackers, welcome to QuantCo's _Claim to Fame_ challenge!
4	
5	---
6	
7	## 🎭 Scenario
8	
9	In insurances, a _claim_ is a request by a policyholder asking for payment or financial compensation. After property damage or a car accident, tradespeople such as handymen and repair garages issue invoices. Policyholders submit these invoices to their insurance providers, which decide whether to pay.
10	
11	But not everyone is honest, so for each invoiced item the insurer must judge whether it is:
12	
13	- **Covered** by the policy,
14	- **Related** to the reported damage, and
15	- **Reasonably** priced (we refer to "total" price per line item in this challenge = quantity * unit price)
16	
17	A fraudulent claim fails one of these: it isn't insured, the item is unrelated to the case, or the price is inflated.
18	
19	## 🎯 Your Task
20	
21	In this challenge you're competing against other teams in rounds. Your goal is to **a) maximize the amount of money you make** and **b) do so with style**.
22	
23	In this challenge, you will take on two roles simultaneously:
24	
25	| Role                             | What you do                                                                                                                                                    |
26	| -------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
27	| 🧾 **Invoice Issuer (Handyman)** | Set the price (= quantity * unit price) for each line item on the invoice that you think you're entitled to. If you set a fair price, you will get your money! |
28	| 🔍 **Insurance Claim Handling**  | Review incoming invoices and minimize the amount your team pays. Spot fraudulent items and set a maximum fair price above which you reject payments.           |
29	
30	In every round, you submit the prices a and b for all items, your submissions will be matched against all other teams.
31	
32	> ⚠️ **But bear in mind:** you can't charge or pay whatever you like. There is a **fair value threshold `t`** for each item. If you reject a request that was at or below this value, you will get a penalty.
33	
34	## 🎲 The Game
35	
36	In regular intervals, a case will be released. You then have _exactly one minute_ to submit. Once the case is released, you will be able to fetch a _decryption key_ from the API. This can then be used to decrypt the `.zip` file for the case. Each case consists of:
37	
38	| File              | Contents                                            |
39	| ----------------- | --------------------------------------------------- |
40	| `policy.txt`      | An **insurance policy** describing what is covered  |
41	| `description.txt` | A **damage description** explaining the claim       |
42	| `invoices.pdf`    | An **invoice** containing line items without prices |
43	| `images.png`      | Some cases might also contain **images**            |
44	
45	After decrypting and extracting, you should analyze the files and set two values for every line item:
46	
47	- **Charge price (`a`)**: the amount you charge opposing teams. _Default: `0`_
48	- **Acceptance limit (`b`)**: the maximum amount your team is willing to accept and pay when receiving the same line item from another team. _Default: `0`_
49	
50	> 💶 **Always submit the _gross total_.** Both the charge price `a` and the acceptance limit `b` must always be given as the gross total for the whole line item. Never the net amount, and never a per-unit price.
51	
52	As mentioned, there will be a **secret threshold (`t`) representing the maximum price that a claims expert would consider appropriate**. For line items that are **not covered** by the policy: `t = 0`.
53	
54	### 💸 Payoffs
55	
56	In the following: `H` is the handyman who issues the invoice, `I` is the insurance that does the claim handling and invoice checking.
57	
58	Everything hinges on where the charge price `a` falls relative to the secret threshold `t`. Picture it on a number line:
59	
60	```
61	        fair zone  (a ≤ t)         │      fraud zone  (a > t)
62	  ◀────────────────────────────────┼───────────────────────────────▶
63	  0                                t                                 a →
64	  the price is valid; H is owed it │ the price is inflated; H is not owed it
65	```
66	
67	- **Left of `t`, the fair zone (`a ≤ t`).** The charge is legitimate, so `H` is entitled to the money. `I` _should_ accept: accepting pays the fair `a`, while rejecting still owes `H` the `a` **plus** a `0.5a` lawyer penalty on `I`.
68	- **Right of `t`, the fraud zone (`a > t`).** The charge is inflated, so `H` is not owed anything. `I` _should_ reject: rejecting means no money flows, while accepting hands `H` the fraudulent amount.
69	
70	The threshold `t` is the dividing line between the two, and it's secret; both roles are really betting on which side of `t` each price sits.
71	
72	> 🧢 **Accepted-payment cap.** Each line item has a secret payment cap c, shared across all teams, where `c ≥ 4t` (and never below an absolute floor). If a charge is accepted, the insurer pays and the issuer receives min(a,c). This prevents teams from winning through a single exorbitantly high charge.
73	
74	The table below details what happens for each transaction.
75	
76	|                            | `a ≤ t`: price okay               | `a > t`: price fraudulent                  |
77	| -------------------------- | --------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------ |
78	| **`a ≤ b` price accepted** | `I` pays `a`, `H` gets `a`        | `I` pays `min(a, c)`, `H` gets `min(a, c)` |
79	| **`a > b` price rejected** | `I` pays `a + 0.5a`, `H` gets `a` | `I` pays `0`, `H` gets `0`                 |
80	
81	**Left column (`a ≤ t`): the price is valid.**
82	
83	- If insurance `I` accepts (`a ≤ b`), it pays the claim: `I` pays `a`, `H` gets `a`.
84	- If insurance `I` wrongfully rejects (`a > b`), `H` still gets the `a` it is owed, but `I` also pays a lawyer as a penalty `0.5a`, so `I` pays `1.5a` in total.
85	
86	**Right column (`a > t`): the price is fraudulent.**
87	
88	- If insurance `I` accepts (`a ≤ b`), `H` is in luck and pockets the capped fraudulent amount `min(a, c)`.
89	- If insurance `I` rightfully rejects (`a > b`), no money flows.
90	
91	## 🧮 An example round
92	
93	Let's walk through a single round with three teams (**Alpha Squad**, **Beta Dynamics**, and **Delta Strategies**) and just **one line item**: a replacement windshield. Suppose the secret fair value threshold for this item is `t = 100`.
94	
95	The game starts at 19:00:00. Teams then have exactly one minute to fetch the decryption key, decrypt the zip file, analyze it and submit they charge price `a` and acceptance limit `b`.
96	Suppose the teams submit:
97	
98	| Team             | Charge `a` | Acceptance limit `b` |
99	| ---------------- | ---------- | -------------------- |
100	| Alpha Squad      | `100`      | `130`                |
101	| Beta Dynamics    | `150`      | `90`                 |
102	| Delta Strategies | `100`      | `110`                |
103	
104	Every team is matched against every other team, in both roles. For each matchup, the **issuer** acts as the handyman `H` (charging its `a`) and the **reviewer** acts as the insurance `I` (deciding with its `b`). That gives six transactions:
105	
106	| Issuer (H) → Reviewer (I) | `a`   | Reviewer's `b` | `a ≤ t`? | `a ≤ b`?  | Outcome                                                   |
107	| ------------------------- | ----- | -------------- | -------- | --------- | --------------------------------------------------------- |
108	| Alpha → Beta              | `100` | `90`           | ✅ okay  | ❌ reject | Wrongful reject: Beta pays `1.5a = 150`, Alpha gets `100` |
109	| Alpha → Delta             | `100` | `110`          | ✅ okay  | ✅ accept | Delta pays `100`, Alpha gets `100`                        |
110	| Delta → Alpha             | `100` | `130`          | ✅ okay  | ✅ accept | Alpha pays `100`, Delta gets `100`                        |
111	| Delta → Beta              | `100` | `90`           | ✅ okay  | ❌ reject | Wrongful reject: Beta pays `1.5a = 150`, Delta gets `100` |
112	| Beta → Alpha              | `150` | `130`          | ❌ fraud | ❌ reject | Rightful reject: no money flows                           |
113	| Beta → Delta              | `150` | `110`          | ❌ fraud | ❌ reject | Rightful reject: no money flows                           |
114	
115	Adding up what each team **gets** (as customer) minus what it **pays** (as insurance):
116	
117	| Team             | Gets  | Pays  | **Net**    |
118	| ---------------- | ----- | ----- | ---------- |
119	| Alpha Squad      | `200` | `100` | **`+100`** |
120	| Delta Strategies | `200` | `100` | **`+100`** |
121	| Beta Dynamics    | `0`   | `300` | **`−300`** |
122	
123	The lesson: **Beta Dynamics loses on both sides.** As a customer it overcharged (`a = 150 > t`), so its fraudulent claims were rightfully rejected and it earned nothing. As an insurance it set its acceptance limit too low (`b = 90 < t`), so it wrongfully rejected fair claims and paid the `1.5a` lawyer penalty + compensation twice. Alpha and Delta both charged fairly and set acceptance limits above the threshold, so they collected their money and avoided penalties.

6	fix that because the errors point in opposite directions. So hand the model the evidence
7	instead: the observed t brackets, grouped by the same buckets c2f.price uses, plus the

20	from c2f.accuracy import rows
21	
22	MIN_N = 3  # a bucket needs this many observations before it is worth a line
23	MIN_PAIRED = 3  # ...and this many carrying BOTH bounds before we quote a two-sided band
24	MAX_LABELS = 12  # recurring labels listed verbatim, most-seen first
25	
26	
27	def _norm(s: str) -> str:
28	    return re.sub(r"[^a-z0-9 ]", "", s.lower()).strip()
29	
30	
31	def _band(obs: list[dict]) -> tuple[float, float | None, int]:
32	    """Both ends of the band measured over the SAME items, and price signal only.
33	
34	    Two things went wrong when the ends were medians over whatever happened to carry each
35	    bound. (1) The subsets are disjoint - ancillary/call-out had 23 floors and 32 ceilings
36	    but only 13 items with both - so the printed ceiling landed UNDER the printed floor in
37	    every bucket, while no single item is inverted (0 of 104). (2) A t_hi on an item with
38	    no proven floor is a COVERAGE refusal, not a price ceiling: the market refused it at
39	    any price. Those were 69 of 173 ceilings and their median is 41 against 184 for real
40	    ones, so pooling them taught the model to under-price the covered items too.
41	
42	    So: only items proven to be worth something carry price signal, and a two-sided band is
43	    quoted only from the items carrying both bounds. Returns (lo, hi, n_behind_the_band).
44	    """
45	    priced = [r for r in obs if r["t_lo"] > 0]
46	    if not priced:
47	        return 0.0, None, 0
48	    paired = [r for r in priced if r["t_hi"] is not None]
49	    if len(paired) >= MIN_PAIRED:
50	        return (
51	            statistics.median(r["t_lo"] for r in paired),
52	            statistics.median(r["t_hi"] for r in paired),
53	            len(paired),
54	        )
55	    return statistics.median(r["t_lo"] for r in priced), None, len(priced)
56	
57	
58	def _fmt(lo: float, hi: float | None, n: int) -> str:
59	    """Never print a range whose ends were not measured on the same items."""
60	    if lo > 0 and hi is not None:
61	        return f"fair value sat between ~EUR {lo:.0f} and ~EUR {hi:.0f}  (n={n} with both bounds)"
62	    if lo > 0:
63	        return f"paid at least ~EUR {lo:.0f}, never refused  (n={n})"
64	    return "no price signal - every observation was refused as not covered"
65	
66	
67	def build() -> str:
68	    try:
69	        R = [r for r in rows() if r["description"].strip()]
70	    except Exception:
71	        return ""
72	    if not R:
73	        return ""
74	
75	    lines: list[str] = []
76	    by_bucket = collections.defaultdict(list)
77	    for r in R:
78	        by_bucket[r["bucket"]].append(r)
79	    for b, obs in sorted(by_bucket.items(), key=lambda x: -len(x[1])):
80	        if b == "other" or len(obs) < MIN_N:
81	            continue
82	        lo, hi, n = _band(obs)
83	        rng = _fmt(lo, hi, n)
84	        # ratio of what the market proved to what we guessed: >1 = we came in too low
85	        ratios = sorted(r["t_lo"] / r["t_mid"] for r in obs if r["t_mid"] > 0 and r["t_lo"] > 0)
86	        hint = ""
87	        if len(ratios) >= MIN_N:
88	            med = ratios[len(ratios) // 2]
89	            if med >= 1.2:
90	                hint = "  (we habitually UNDER-price this category)"
91	            elif med <= 0.8:
92	                hint = "  (we habitually OVER-price this category)"
93	        lines.append(f"  {b:<20} {rng}{hint}")
94	
95	    by_label = collections.defaultdict(list)
96	    for r in R:
97	        by_label[_norm(r["description"])].append(r)
98	    repeats = sorted(
99	        ((k, v) for k, v in by_label.items() if len({x["game"] for x in v}) > 1),
100	        key=lambda x: -len(x[1]),
101	    )[:MAX_LABELS]
102	    label_lines = []
103	    for k, obs in repeats:
104	        lo, hi, n = _band(obs)
105	        label_lines.append(f"  {k[:38]:<40} {_fmt(lo, hi, n)}")
106	
107	    if not lines and not label_lines:
108	        return ""
109	    out = (
110	        '<market_history note="what the market ACTUALLY accepted for comparable line items in '
111	        'past rounds of THIS game, recovered from the opponents\' charges. Evidence, not a rule: '
112	        'this case\'s policy and quantities still decide. Use it to sanity-check the ORDER OF '
113	        'MAGNITUDE of your t_mid, and be reluctant to land far outside a range with many '
114	        'observations behind it.">\n'
115	    )
116	    if lines:
117	        out += "by category:\n" + "\n".join(lines) + "\n"
118	    if label_lines:

120	    return out + "</market_history>\n\n"

## Key Research Findings

**Overconfidence in LLM Confidence Intervals:**

Large language models excel at numerical estimation but struggle to correctly quantify uncertainty, and when constructing confidence intervals around their own answers, they are systematically overconfident.

**FermiEval Benchmark:**

A recent benchmark called FermiEval evaluates confidence interval coverage and sharpness using Fermi-style estimation questions, finding that nominal 99% intervals cover the true answer only 65% of the time on average across several modern models.

**Calibration Solutions:**

Conformal prediction-based approaches can adjust intervals to obtain accurate 99% observed coverage with a 54% decrease in Winkler interval score, and direct log-probability elicitation and quantile adjustment methods further reduce overconfidence at high confidence levels.

**Verbalized Confidence Issues:**

When verbalizing their confidence, LLMs tend to be overconfident, potentially imitating human patterns of expressing confidence. Additionally, verbalized scores often remain overconfident without further alignment.

**Methods to Improve Calibration:**

Prompting strategies such as Chain-of-Thought (CoT), Top-K, and Multi-step confidences improve calibration of verbalized confidence, and hybrid methods consistently deliver the best performance.

The research indicates this is an active area of study with multiple proposed solutions including conformal prediction, quantile elicitation, and improved prompting strategies.

## Key Findings:

**Turnbull Estimator Fundamentals:**
The Turnbull estimator is a nonparametric maximum likelihood estimator of a one-dimensional distribution based on N independent, arbitrarily censored and/or truncated observations (including interval censoring). Turnbull derived the nonparametric maximum likelihood estimator (NPMLE) under arbitrary interval-censoring, which is obtained via an expectation-maximization (EM) procedure and allocates mass to a set of disjoint intervals, commonly referred to as "Turnbull intervals" and is fully data-driven without imposing structural assumptions on the hazard.

**Parametric Approaches with Lognormal:**
Weibull and log-normal accelerated failure time (AFT) models with interval likelihoods provide smooth, covariate-adjusted survival curves and interpretable time-ratio effects. Parametric approaches, such as accelerated failure time (AFT) models with Weibull or log-normal distributions, yield smooth curves, admit covariates, and provide interpretable regression effects.

**Robust Estimation with Heavy Tails:**
For incomplete loss data, robust estimation approaches have been developed, including MTM (Method of Trimmed Moments) estimators of the lognormal distribution parameters, and MTM is the most effective approach for robust estimation of truncated and censored lognormal models.
