Research complete. Here's the full assessment.

# How t, a, b are produced today — and why it's losing money

## The current pipeline

**t** — one LLM call per case ([llm.py](c2f/llm.py)'s `SYSTEM`) returns `t_low/t_mid/t_high` per item. The prompt repeatedly instructs frugality: *"Claims experts are frugal: when unsure, go lower"*, *"price the CHEAPEST reasonable standard replacement"*, *"make t_low 2-3x lower than t_mid"*, plus hard-coded anchors ("diagnostic typically €50–300", "a 2-hour job ~€50–150").

**Belief** — [price.py:207](c2f/price.py#L207) builds a lognormal with median `t_mid × bias` (per-bucket bias where labelled) and `sigma = max(calibrated σ, model spread)`. `bias` and `σ` come from an interval-censored MLE in [calibrate.py:85](c2f/calibrate.py#L85) over the `[t_lo, t_hi)` brackets recovered after each game.

**b** = 1/3-quantile of the belief (from the 1.5×-vs-1× reject/accept asymmetry). **a** = grid-maximizer of `mean − 0.55·sd` of per-opponent payout, capped at the belief median, with fraud acceptance decaying as `p0·(a/t)^−k`.

## What the data says is broken

The decision rules for a and b are fine given a good belief. **The belief is the problem, in three compounding ways:**

**1. σ is railing at its clamp (1.0) — the point estimate is nearly uninformative.** [calibration.json](runs/calibration.json) shows `sigma: 1.0`, the exact top of `SIGMA_RANGE`. A log-sd of 1.0 means the 80% belief interval spans ~13×. That forces deep shading everywhere: b ≈ 0.65×median, a ≈ 0.5–0.7×median — which is exactly the game-35 postmortem: ~€12.5k regret from b refusing proven-fair charges and ~€25.5k of a left on the table (repriced window in [deviation.json](runs/deviation.json)), and game 35 itself net −€8,179.

**2. The bias isn't a constant multiplier — it's a slope.** I split the 184 labels by size:

| t_mid size | n | median t_lo/t_mid | share with t_lo > t_mid |
|---|---|---|---|
| < €100 | 54 | **×1.51** | 76% |
| €100–400 | 81 | ×1.05 | 58% |
| ≥ €400 | 49 | **×0.86** | 39% |

Small items are badly underestimated; large items slightly over. On the 118 double-bounded labels, `log t = 1.74 + 0.66·log t_mid` fits with residual sd 0.73, vs 0.84 for the pure-bias model — and the pure-bias fit on that subset gives ×0.93 while the censored MLE over all labels gives ×1.52. Those two can't both be right under the current model; that contradiction is *why* σ inflates to the rail. The single `bias` multiplier is structurally the wrong shape (the per-bucket biases — labour 1.82, material 1.99 — are partly just proxying "small-ticket bucket").

**3. The prompt is fighting the market — and its own evidence block.** Game 35's worst items make it concrete:

- Items 12–14 (copper elbows, qty 5): the model answered *"One standard 28mm elbow reasonably allowed, not five"* → t_mid 15 vs. proven t ≥ 96. The *"price only the QUANTITY needed... never the full invoice quantity"* directive was written for duplicate call-out fees, but it fires on material lines — while the game defines t over the line **as invoiced** (qty × unit price), and the market accepted all five elbows.
- Item 7 "Room dryer unit": t_mid 170, while the model's own `<market_history>` block said *"room dryer unit paid at least ~EUR 359"*. Item 1 "Indoor leak detection": t_mid 410 vs. history's *"paid at least ~EUR 460"*. The frugality instructions in SYSTEM are overriding the empirical evidence the prompt itself supplies, and the hard-coded "€50–300 diagnostic" anchor directly contradicts history's €230–274 band.

Then the math multiplies everything by 1.52 to compensate — which overcorrects the items the model got right (game 35 item 1: a=777 charged past the €777 ceiling, −€6,844; item 15: b=945 accepted fraud above the €709 ceiling, −€4,691). Prompting down + multiplying back up = maximum variance, and variance is what σ=1.0 is measuring.

## What research and industry practice say

- **LLM verbalized intervals are systematically overconfident** — [FermiEval (arXiv 2510.26995)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.26995) finds nominal 99% intervals cover only ~65%; the effective fixes are post-hoc: conformal quantile adjustment cut interval loss ~54%. Also [Can LLMs Express Their Uncertainty? (arXiv 2306.13063)](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2306.13063) and [On Verbalized Confidence Scores](https://arxiv.org/html/2412.14737v2). Implication: **don't ask the model to be conservative — ask for its honest quantiles and calibrate them in code**, which you already have the machinery for.
- **Conformal/split-calibration is the industry standard** for turning point predictions into honest intervals with coverage guarantees ([awesome-conformal-prediction](https://github.com/valeman/awesome-conformal-prediction), [Self-Calibrating Conformal Prediction](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2402.07307)). Your 184 labels are exactly the calibration set this needs.
- **Interval-censored parametric fits (lognormal AFT with covariates)** are the standard for bracket-only labels ([robust survival estimation under interval censoring, arXiv 2509.02634](https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.02634)) — an AFT with `log t_mid` as covariate is precisely the slope model above, and it handles your one-sided brackets properly where my quick regression couldn't.
- **Bid shading literature** ([Bid Shading in First-Price Auctions](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2009.01360), [distributionally-robust shading](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2410.14864)) optimizes against the **empirical opponent distribution**, not a parametric acceptance curve. You have `runs/feed/g35_*.json` per opponent — the `p0·r^−k` fit (currently k=0.6, fitted only on proven-fraud points, a biased sample) could be replaced by directly simulating a against recovered opponent b's.
- **Self-consistency** (median of k samples) helps numeric estimation but plateaus fast and costs latency ([arXiv 2511.00751](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2511.00751)) — with a 60s clock, at most median-of-2/3 on the chunked calls; lower priority than the fixes above.

## Recommendations, ranked by expected impact

1. **Prompt: fix the quantity rule.** Restrict "price only ONE" to duplicate call-out/inspection *fees*; state explicitly that t is the threshold for the line **as invoiced** — materials and hours keep their invoiced quantity unless the quantity itself is unjustified. Items 12–14 alone were ~€4.5k of game-35 regret.
2. **Prompt: drop the frugality slant and stale anchors.** Replace "claims experts are frugal, go lower" with "estimate the threshold a German claims expert would still accept — market evidence shows accepted prices run at or above typical mid-market gross rates", delete the €50–300-style hard anchors that contradict `<market_history>`, and strengthen history from "be reluctant to land far outside" to "when a verbatim label match exists, your t_mid must not sit below its proven floor without stating why".
3. **Math: replace the constant bias with an affine-in-log calibration** `log t̂ = α + β·log t_mid (+ bucket offset)`, fitted by the same interval-censored MLE (it's a 3-parameter grid instead of 2). Expect σ to drop well below 1.0, which automatically raises both a and b out of the over-shaded regime. Treat σ hitting the clamp as an alert, not a value.
4. **Math: heteroscedastic σ** — fit σ per size band (small items genuinely are noisier) so big items aren't punished with small-item uncertainty.
5. **Math: empirical acceptance curve** — replace `p0·r^−k` in `best_charge` with simulation against the recovered opponent limits from the feed files (your backtest already has them).
6. Optional: median-of-2 sampling per chunk if the clock allows; keep `MODEL_SPREAD_Z` but re-read t_low/t_high as honest P10/P90 once instruction (2) stops skewing t_low.

Note the interaction: fixes 1–2 raise raw t_mid, so the current bias=1.52 would then overshoot — **recalibrate immediately after any prompt change** (the affine fit in 3 makes that safe, since it can learn slope ≈ 1, intercept ≈ 0 if the prompt fix lands).

Sources: [FermiEval — LLMs are Overconfident](https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.26995) · [Can LLMs Express Their Uncertainty?](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2306.13063) · [On Verbalized Confidence Scores](https://arxiv.org/html/2412.14737v2) · [Self-Calibrating Conformal Prediction](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2402.07307) · [awesome-conformal-prediction](https://github.com/valeman/awesome-conformal-prediction) · [Robust Survival Estimation under Interval Censoring](https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.02634) · [Bid Shading in First-Price Auctions](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2009.01360) · [Double Distributionally Robust Bid Shading](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2410.14864) · [Self-Consistency Is Losing Its Edge](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2511.00751)

Want me to implement any of these? The highest-value, lowest-risk pair is (1)+(3): the quantity-rule prompt fix plus the affine calibration, gated on `make backtest` per your workflow.
Try the solutions and see how they perform on the previous rounds
I'll implement the fixes and score them on past rounds. First, per the project rules, let me read AGENTS.md and the evaluation tooling before touching code.

1	"""Replay the CURRENT strategy on past games and score it against what the other teams actually did.
2	
3	  pixi run python -m c2f.backtest              # re-price + re-score every stored replay; NO model call
4	  pixi run python -m c2f.backtest --replay     # call the model again for every old game, then score
5	  pixi run python -m c2f.backtest --replay 2 4 # call the model for these games only; others from store
6	
7	The default never calls the model: each old game's stored model estimate (runs/backtest/game_NN.json)
8	is re-priced with the CURRENT price.py + calibration and re-scored, so pricing changes are evaluated
9	in seconds. --replay is for changes upstream of pricing (prompt, extract, policy digest).
10	
11	Per game:  extract -> digest -> model (same code path as a live run) -> price -> simulate every pairing
12	against the real opponents of that round, using the public leaderboard:
13	  - each opponent's charge a_j per item and whether it was fair (from payouts),
14	  - each opponent's accept limit b_j as an interval [b_lo, b_hi) (from what they accepted/rejected),
15	  - the fair value t as an interval [t_lo, t_hi) (largest charge proven fair, smallest proven fraud).
16	Where an interval leaves the outcome open we score two scenarios: PESSIMISTIC (t = t_lo, opponents
17	reject whenever they could) and OPTIMISTIC (t just under t_hi, opponents accept whenever they could).
18	Our rank = where our replayed net would have put us in that round's standings.
19	
20	THE BAR IS MONEY, AND ONLY MONEY. EXPECTED = midpoint of the two scenarios; a change is a SUCCESS
21	when the expected replay is PROFITABLE (net > 0) in more than half of the old games and the total
22	expected net is positive. Rank is reported but does not gate: a steady 3rd place every round while
23	in profit is exactly the target outcome, so we never fail a strategy for not topping the table.
24	The population is the LAST 10 completed games whose case is decrypted locally (WINDOW), not just the
25	games replayed in this invocation: games you don't name are re-scored from their stored replay (no
26	model call), games with no stored replay count as a failure and are listed as missing.
27	
28	This is THE evaluation entry point. It uses the other tools as components:
29	  feedback.digest  -> opponents' charges, accept/reject, payout-based t bounds
30	  truth.infer      -> tighter t bounds from the matchup cells (cached in runs/truth_game_NN.json)
31	  calibration.json -> reported alongside, so a result is tied to the calibration it ran with
32	Writes runs/backtest/game_NN.json and runs/backtest/summary.json (+ a table on stdout). Nothing
33	enforces the verdict - run this when a change is worth checking and read the table.
34	"""
35	
36	from __future__ import annotations
37	
38	import argparse
39	import json
40	import sys
41	import time
42	from pathlib import Path
43	
44	import requests
45	
46	from c2f import llm
47	from c2f.extract import load_case
48	from c2f.feedback import B, DEFAULT_TEAM, digest
49	from c2f.policy import attach as attach_policy_digest
50	from c2f.price import price_all
51	from c2f.run import merge_estimates
52	from c2f.submit import ROOT
53	from c2f import truth as truth_mod
54	
55	OUT = ROOT / "runs" / "backtest"
56	INF = float("inf")
57	WINDOW = 10  # the verdict is over the LAST 10 completed games with a decrypted case
58	RANK_TARGET = 3  # top-3 is the outcome we aim for; reported only - the verdict gates on money
59	
60	
61	# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- evidence
62	def t_bounds(game_id: int, d: dict) -> dict:
63	    """Tightest fair-value bounds per item: payout evidence (feedback.digest) merged with the
64	    matchup-cell inference (truth.py). truth results are cached in runs/truth_game_NN.json."""
65	    p = ROOT / "runs" / f"truth_game_{game_id:02d}.json"
66	    tr: dict = {}
67	    if p.exists():
68	        tr = json.loads(p.read_text())
69	    else:
70	        try:
71	            tr = {str(k): v for k, v in truth_mod.infer(game_id).items()}
72	            p.write_text(json.dumps(tr, indent=1))
73	        except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001 - truth is best-effort; payout bounds still apply
74	            print(f"   (truth inference unavailable for game {game_id}: {e.__class__.__name__})")
75	    src = {}
76	    for i in d["items"]:
77	        lo, hi = d["t_lo"][i], d["t_hi"][i]
78	        v = tr.get(str(i))
79	        if v:
80	            lo = max(lo, float(v.get("t_lo") or 0.0))
81	            if v.get("t_hi") is not None:
82	                hi = min(hi, float(v["t_hi"]))
83	        d["t_lo"][i], d["t_hi"][i] = lo, hi
84	        src[i] = "truth+payout" if v else "payout"
85	    return src
86	
87	
88	# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- replay
89	def replay(game_id: int) -> dict:
90	    """One model call, exactly as run.py plays it."""
91	    case_dir = ROOT / "cases" / f"case_{game_id:02d}"
92	    case = load_case(case_dir, game_id)
93	    attach_policy_digest(case, case_dir)  # same prompt the live run would build
94	    t0 = time.time()
95	    out, _meta = llm.estimate(case, timeout=60, strict=False)
96	    rows = price_all(merge_estimates(case, out))
97	    return {"rows": rows, "estimate": out, "seconds": round(time.time() - t0, 1)}
98	
99	
100	def reprice(game_id: int, rep: dict) -> dict:
101	    """Price the stored model estimate with the current price.py + calibration; no model call."""
102	    est = rep.get("estimate") or rep.get("ensemble")
103	    if not est:
104	        return rep
105	    case = load_case(ROOT / "cases" / f"case_{game_id:02d}", game_id)
106	    return {**rep, "rows": price_all(merge_estimates(case, est)), "repriced": True}
107	
108	
109	# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- scoring
110	def _fair_status(a: float, t_lo: float, t_hi: float) -> bool | None:
111	    """True = proven fair, False = proven fraud, None = open."""
112	    if a <= 0:
113	        return True
114	    if a <= t_lo + 1e-9:
115	        return True
116	    if a >= t_hi - 1e-9:
117	        return False
118	    return None
119	
120	
121	def score(game_id: int, rows: list[dict], d: dict, us: str) -> dict:
122	    ours = {r["index"]: (r["charge_price"], r["acceptance_limit"]) for r in rows}
123	    opp = [t for t in d["teams"] if t != us]
124	    res = {"pessimistic": {"income": 0.0, "cost": 0.0}, "optimistic": {"income": 0.0, "cost": 0.0}}
125	    open_income = open_cost = 0
126	    per_item = {}
127	    for i in d["items"]:
128	        a, b = ours.get(i, (0.0, 0.0))
129	        t_lo, t_hi = d["t_lo"][i], d["t_hi"][i]
130	        fair_ours = _fair_status(a, t_lo, t_hi)
131	        inc = {"pessimistic": 0.0, "optimistic": 0.0}
132	        cost = {"pessimistic": 0.0, "optimistic": 0.0}
133	        for j in opp:
134	            # ---- we issue a to reviewer j
135	            b_lo, b_hi = d["b_lo"][j].get(i, 0.0), d["b_hi"][j].get(i, INF)
136	            acc = True if a <= b_lo + 1e-9 else (False if a >= b_hi - 1e-9 else None)
137	            for sc in ("pessimistic", "optimistic"):
138	                fair = fair_ours if fair_ours is not None else (sc == "optimistic")
139	                accepted = acc if acc is not None else (sc == "optimistic")
140	                if fair:
141	                    inc[sc] += a
142	                elif accepted:
143	                    inc[sc] += a  # cap assumed not binding
144	            if fair_ours is None or acc is None:
145	                open_income += 1
146	            # ---- j issues a_j to us
147	            a_j = d["issued"][j].get(i)
148	            if a_j is None or a_j <= 0:
149	                # unknown charge (rejected by everyone, paid 0 => fraud, a_j > 0 unknown) or a_j = 0
150	                # we only pay it if our b >= a_j; a_j unknown but every team rejected it, assume we do too
151	                continue
152	            fair_j = d["fair"][j].get(i)
153	            if fair_j is None:
154	                fair_j = _fair_status(a_j, t_lo, t_hi)
155	            we_accept = a_j <= b + 1e-9
156	            for sc in ("pessimistic", "optimistic"):
157	                fair = fair_j if fair_j is not None else (sc == "pessimistic")
158	                if fair:
159	                    cost[sc] += a_j if we_accept else 1.5 * a_j
160	                elif we_accept:
161	                    cost[sc] += a_j
162	            if fair_j is None:
163	                open_cost += 1
164	        for sc in res:
165	            res[sc]["income"] += inc[sc]
166	            res[sc]["cost"] += cost[sc]
167	        per_item[i] = {"a": a, "b": b, "t_lo": t_lo, "t_hi": None if t_hi == INF else t_hi, "fair": fair_ours,
168	                       "income": inc, "cost": cost}
169	    for sc in res:
170	        res[sc]["net"] = round(res[sc]["income"] - res[sc]["cost"], 2)
171	        res[sc]["income"] = round(res[sc]["income"], 2)
172	        res[sc]["cost"] = round(res[sc]["cost"], 2)
173	    return {"scenarios": res, "open_pairings": {"income": open_income, "cost": open_cost}, "items": per_item}
174	
175	
176	def actual_nets() -> tuple[list[int], dict[str, dict[int, float]]]:
177	    m = requests.get(f"{B}/matrix?page=1&game_limit=1000", timeout=20).json()
178	    gids = m["game_ids"]
179	    nets = {row["team_name"]: {g: c for g, c in zip(gids, row["cells"])} for row in m["items"]}
180	    return gids, nets
181	
182	
183	def rank_of(net: float, others: list[float]) -> int:
184	    return 1 + sum(1 for x in others if x > net)
185	
186	
187	def old_games(gids: list[int], window: int = WINDOW) -> list[int]:
188	    """The population the verdict is over: the last `window` completed games whose case is
189	    decrypted locally (older games drift - other teams change strategy between rounds)."""
190	    have = sorted(g for g in gids if (ROOT / "cases" / f"case_{g:02d}" / "policy.txt").exists())
191	    return have[-window:]
192	
193	
194	def verdict(games: dict, old: list[int]) -> dict:
195	    """Totals + SUCCESS flag over the full set of old games. `games` holds the per-game rows we have
196	    (replayed now or re-scored from the store); old games without a row count as a failure.
197	
198	    The bar is MONEY, and only money: a game counts when the expected replay net is positive.
199	    Rank is reported (`top_ranked`, `good`, `wins_exp`) but does NOT gate the verdict - placing
200	    3rd every round while in profit is the target outcome, so a strategy that pays in every game
201	    passes even if it never tops the table.
202	    """
203	    rows = [games[g] for g in old if g in games]
204	    missing = [g for g in old if g not in games]
205	    n = len(old)
206	    paid = sum(1 for v in rows if v["exp_net"] > 0)
207	    top = sum(1 for v in rows if v["exp_rank"] <= RANK_TARGET)
208	    good = sum(1 for v in rows if v["exp_net"] > 0 and v["exp_rank"] <= RANK_TARGET)
209	    return {
210	        "actual": sum(v["actual_net"] for v in rows), "pessimistic": sum(v["pess_net"] for v in rows),
211	        "expected": sum(v["exp_net"] for v in rows), "optimistic": sum(v["opt_net"] for v in rows),
212	        "profitable": paid, "top_ranked": top, "good": good, "rank_target": RANK_TARGET,
213	        "wins_pess": sum(1 for v in rows if v["pess_rank"] == 1),
214	        "wins_exp": sum(1 for v in rows if v["exp_rank"] == 1),
215	        "wins_opt": sum(1 for v in rows if v["opt_rank"] == 1),
216	        "n_games": n, "n_scored": len(rows), "missing": missing,
217	        "success": n > 0 and not missing and paid * 2 > n and sum(v["exp_net"] for v in rows) > 0,
218	    }
219	
220	
221	# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- main
222	def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
223	    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
224	    ap.add_argument("games", nargs="*", type=int)
225	    ap.add_argument("--replay", action="store_true", help="call the model for the named games (default: all old games); otherwise stored estimates are re-priced")
226	    ap.add_argument("--no-llm", action="store_true", help=argparse.SUPPRESS)  # old spelling of the default
227	    args = ap.parse_args(argv)
228	
229	    OUT.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
230	    gids, nets = actual_nets()
231	    us = DEFAULT_TEAM
232	    old = old_games(gids)
233	    requested = args.games or old
234	    # every old game is scored: with --replay the requested ones call the model, everything else is
235	    # re-priced from its stored estimate (no model call)
236	    for g in requested:
237	        if g not in gids:
238	            print(f"{g:>4}  not completed yet, skipped")
239	        elif g not in old:
240	            print(f"{g:>4}  not in the last {WINDOW} decrypted games {old} (or not decrypted), skipped")
241	    plan = [(g, args.replay and g in requested) for g in old]
242	    summary = {"team": us, "games": {}, "old_games": old, "generated_at": time.time()}
243	    print(f"backtest as {us}: {len(old)} old games {old}, replaying {[g for g, r in plan if r]}\n")
244	    print(f"{'game':>4} {'items':>5} | {'actual net':>10} {'rank':>4} | {'replay pess':>11} {'rank':>4} | {'replay exp':>10} {'rank':>4} | {'replay opt':>10} {'rank':>4} | best team")
245	    for g, do_replay in plan:
246	        path = OUT / f"game_{g:02d}.json"
247	        if do_replay:
248	            rep = replay(g)
249	        elif path.exists():
250	            rep = reprice(g, json.loads(path.read_text())["replay"])
251	        else:
252	            print(f"{g:>4}  no stored replay - MISSING, counts as not won (run: make replay G={g})")
253	            continue
254	        d = digest(g)
255	        evidence = t_bounds(g, d)
256	        sc = score(g, rep["rows"], d, us)
257	        sc["evidence"] = evidence
258	        others = [nets[t][g] for t in nets if t != us]
259	        best = max(nets.items(), key=lambda kv: kv[1][g])
260	        actual = nets.get(us, {}).get(g, float("nan"))
261	        exp_net = (sc["scenarios"]["pessimistic"]["net"] + sc["scenarios"]["optimistic"]["net"]) / 2
262	        row = {
263	            "actual_net": actual,
264	            "actual_rank": rank_of(actual, others),
265	            "replay": rep,
266	            "score": sc,
267	            "pess_net": sc["scenarios"]["pessimistic"]["net"],
268	            "pess_rank": rank_of(sc["scenarios"]["pessimistic"]["net"], others),
269	            "opt_net": sc["scenarios"]["optimistic"]["net"],
270	            "opt_rank": rank_of(sc["scenarios"]["optimistic"]["net"], others),
271	            "exp_net": round(exp_net, 2),
272	            "exp_rank": rank_of(exp_net, others),
273	            "best_team": best[0],
274	            "best_net": best[1][g],
275	            "n_teams": len(nets),
276	            "replayed_now": do_replay,
277	        }
278	        path.write_text(json.dumps(row, indent=1, default=str))
279	        summary["games"][g] = {k: v for k, v in row.items() if k not in ("replay", "score")}
280	        tag = "" if do_replay else "  (stored estimate, re-priced)"
281	        print(f"{g:>4} {len(d['items']):>5} | {actual:10.0f} {row['actual_rank']:>4} | {row['pess_net']:11.0f} {row['pess_rank']:>4} | "
282	              f"{row['exp_net']:10.0f} {row['exp_rank']:>4} | {row['opt_net']:10.0f} {row['opt_rank']:>4} | {best[0]} ({best[1][g]:.0f}){tag}")
283	    t = verdict(summary["games"], old)
284	    summary["totals"] = t
285	    n = t["n_games"]
286	    print(f"\ntotal: actual {t['actual']:.0f} | replay pess {t['pessimistic']:.0f} | "
287	          f"exp {t['expected']:.0f} | opt {t['optimistic']:.0f} over {t['n_scored']}/{n} old games")
288	    if t["missing"]:
289	        print(f"MISSING replays for old games {t['missing']} - counted as a failure; run: make replay G=\"{' '.join(map(str, t['missing']))}\"")
290	    print(f"VERDICT: {'SUCCESS' if t['success'] else 'NOT GOOD ENOUGH'} - profitable in "
291	          f"{t['profitable']}/{n} old games (need > {n // 2}), expected net {t['expected']:.0f} "
292	          f"[rank, not gating: top-{RANK_TARGET} {t['top_ranked']}/{n}, outright wins {t['wins_exp']}]")
293	    cal = ROOT / "runs" / "calibration.json"
294	    if cal.exists():
295	        c = json.loads(cal.read_text())
296	        summary["calibration"] = c
297	        print("calibration in effect:", {k: (round(v, 3) if isinstance(v, float) else v) for k, v in c.items() if not isinstance(v, list)})
298	    (OUT / "summary.json").write_text(json.dumps(summary, indent=1, default=str))
299	    print(f"saved {OUT.relative_to(ROOT)}/summary.json")
300	    return 0
301	
302	
303	if __name__ == "__main__":
304	    sys.exit(main())

def _loglik(rows: list[dict], mu: float, sigma: float, beta: float = 1.0) -> float:
    """Interval-censored normal log-likelihood of ln t around the affine-corrected centre
    ln t_mid + mu + (beta - 1) * (ln t_mid - ln PIVOT_T). beta = 1 is the old pure-bias model."""
    ll = 0.0
    lp = math.log(PIVOT_T)
    for r in rows:
        m = math.log(r["t_mid"])
        c = m + mu + (beta - 1.0) * (m - lp)
        lo = _N.cdf((math.log(r["t_lo"]) - c) / sigma) if r["t_lo"] > 0 else 0.0
        hi = _N.cdf((math.log(r["t_hi"]) - c) / sigma) if r["t_hi"] else 1.0
        ll += math.log(max(hi - lo, 1e-9))
    return ll


def fit_bias_sigma(rows: list[dict], beta: float = 1.0) -> tuple[float, float]:
    """rows: {t_lo, t_hi (or None), t_mid>0}. Grid MLE of (bias, sigma) with the slope held fixed."""
    rows = [r for r in rows if r["t_mid"] > 0 and (r["t_lo"] > 0 or r.get("t_hi"))]
    best, best_ll = (0.0, DEFAULT_CALIBRATION.sigma), -math.inf
    mus = [math.log(BIAS_RANGE[0]) + i * (math.log(BIAS_RANGE[1]) - math.log(BIAS_RANGE[0])) / 100 for i in range(101)]
    sigmas = [SIGMA_RANGE[0] + i * (SIGMA_RANGE[1] - SIGMA_RANGE[0]) / 85 for i in range(86)]
    for mu in mus:
        for s in sigmas:
            ll = _loglik(rows, mu, s, beta)
            if ll > best_ll:
                best, best_ll = (mu, s), ll
    return math.exp(best[0]), best[1]


def fit_bias_beta_sigma(rows: list[dict]) -> tuple[float, float, float]:
    """Joint grid MLE of (bias, beta, sigma). Fitting beta jointly matters: under the beta = 1
    model the size-shaped error inflates sigma to its clamp, which then over-shades every price."""
    rows = [r for r in rows if r["t_mid"] > 0 and (r["t_lo"] > 0 or r.get("t_hi"))]
    best, best_ll = (0.0, 1.0, DEFAULT_CALIBRATION.sigma), -math.inf
    mus = [math.log(BIAS_RANGE[0]) + i * (math.log(BIAS_RANGE[1]) - math.log(BIAS_RANGE[0])) / 60 for i in range(61)]
    betas = [BETA_RANGE[0] + i * (BETA_RANGE[1] - BETA_RANGE[0]) / 18 for i in range(19)]
    sigmas = [SIGMA_RANGE[0] + i * (SIGMA_RANGE[1] - SIGMA_RANGE[0]) / 34 for i in range(35)]
    for b in betas:
        for mu in mus:
            for s in sigmas:
                ll = _loglik(rows, mu, s, b)
                if ll > best_ll:
                    best, best_ll = (mu, b, s), ll
    return math.exp(best[0]), best[1], best[2]

input.old_string:
def _loglik(rows: list[dict], mu: float, sigma: float, beta: float = 1.0) -> float:
    """Interval-censored normal log-likelihood of ln t around the affine-corrected centre
    ln t_mid + mu + (beta - 1) * (ln t_mid - ln PIVOT_T). beta = 1 is the old pure-bias model."""
    ll = 0.0
    lp = math.log(PIVOT_T)
    for r in rows:
        m = math.log(r["t_mid"])
        c = m + mu + (beta - 1.0) * (m - lp)
        lo = _N.cdf((math.log(r["t_lo"]) - c) / sigma) if r["t_lo"] > 0 else 0.0
        hi = _N.cdf((math.log(r["t_hi"]) - c) / sigma) if r["t_hi"] else 1.0
        ll += math.log(max(hi - lo, 1e-9))
    return ll


def fit_bias_sigma(rows: list[dict], beta: float = 1.0) -> tuple[float, float]:
    """rows: {t_lo, t_hi (or None), t_mid>0}. Grid MLE of (bias, sigma) with the slope held fixed."""
    rows = [r for r in rows if r["t_mid"] > 0 and (r["t_lo"] > 0 or r.get("t_hi"))]
    best, best_ll = (0.0, DEFAULT_CALIBRATION.sigma), -math.inf
    mus = [math.log(BIAS_RANGE[0]) + i * (math.log(BIAS_RANGE[1]) - math.log(BIAS_RANGE[0])) / 100 for i in range(101)]
    sigmas = [SIGMA_RANGE[0] + i * (SIGMA_RANGE[1] - SIGMA_RANGE[0]) / 85 for i in range(86)]
    for mu in mus:
        for s in sigmas:
            ll = _loglik(rows, mu, s, beta)
            if ll > best_ll:
                best, best_ll = (mu, s), ll
    return math.exp(best[0]), best[1]


def fit_bias_beta_sigma(rows: list[dict]) -> tuple[float, float, float]:
    """Joint grid MLE of (bias, beta, sigma). Fitting beta jointly matters: under the beta = 1
    model the size-shaped error inflates sigma to its clamp, which then over-shades every price."""
    rows = [r for r in rows if r["t_mid"] > 0 and (r["t_lo"] > 0 or r.get("t_hi"))]
    best, best_ll = (0.0, 1.0, DEFAULT_CALIBRATION.sigma), -math.inf
    mus = [math.log(BIAS_RANGE[0]) + i * (math.log(BIAS_RANGE[1]) - math.log(BIAS_RANGE[0])) / 60 for i in range(61)]
    betas = [BETA_RANGE[0] + i * (BETA_RANGE[1] - BETA_RANGE[0]) / 18 for i in range(19)]
    sigmas = [SIGMA_RANGE[0] + i * (SIGMA_RANGE[1] - SIGMA_RANGE[0]) / 34 for i in range(35)]
    for b in betas:
        for mu in mus:
            for s in sigmas:
                ll = _loglik(rows, mu, s, b)
                if ll > best_ll:
                    best, best_ll = (mu, b, s), ll
    return math.exp(best[0]), best[1], best[2]

"""Refit bias/beta/sigma on the NEW-prompt replayed estimates (runs/backtest/game_NN.json)
instead of the live-run estimates, so the calibration matches the prompt that produced them.
Writes runs/calibration.json. p0/k are kept from the current file (they come from feedback,
not from estimates)."""
import json
import sys
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(r"c:\Users\Admin\Desktop\TUM\8.Semester\Hackathon\EHL-Hackathon-template-repo")
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT))

from c2f import calibrate  # noqa: E402
from c2f.extract import case_labels  # noqa: E402
from c2f.price import bucket_of, CALIBRATION_PATH, PIVOT_T  # noqa: E402


def replay_estimates(game_id: int) -> dict[int, dict]:
    p = ROOT / "runs" / "backtest" / f"game_{game_id:02d}.json"
    if not p.exists():
        return {}
    rec = json.loads(p.read_text())
    est = (rec.get("replay") or {}).get("estimate")
    if not est:
        return {}
    items = {int(it["index"]): it for it in est["items"]}
    # recover descriptions for the buckets, same as calibrate.estimates()
    case_p = ROOT / "cases" / f"case_{game_id:02d}"
    try:
        from c2f.extract import load_case
        case = load_case(case_p, game_id)
        descs = case_labels(case)
    except Exception:
        descs = {}
    for i, it in items.items():
        if not it.get("_description"):
            it["_description"] = descs.get(i, "")
    return items


def labels() -> list[dict]:
    rows = []
    for p in sorted((ROOT / "runs").glob("truth_game_*.json")):
        g = int(p.stem.split("_")[-1])
        est = replay_estimates(g)
        if not est:
            continue  # only new-prompt games enter the fit
        truth = json.loads(p.read_text())
        for i, tv in truth.items():
            it = est.get(int(i))
            if not it:
                continue
            lo, hi = float(tv["t_lo"] or 0.0), tv.get("t_hi")
            if lo <= 0 and hi is None:
                continue
            mid = float(it.get("t_mid") or 0)
            covered = bool(it.get("covered")) and bool(it.get("related", True)) and mid > 0
            rows.append({"game": g, "item": int(i), "t_lo": lo, "t_hi": hi, "t_mid": mid,
                         "covered": covered, "bucket": bucket_of(it.get("_description", ""))})
    return rows


rows = labels()
fit_rows = [r for r in rows if r["covered"] and r["t_lo"] > 0]
games = sorted({r["game"] for r in fit_rows})
print(f"{len(fit_rows)} labelled covered items from replayed games {games}")
bias, beta, beta_high, sigma = calibrate.fit_bias_beta_sigma(fit_rows)
print(f"bias {bias:.3f} (at t_mid {PIVOT_T:.0f}), beta {beta:.2f} below / {beta_high:.2f} above, sigma {sigma:.3f}")
buckets = calibrate.fit_bucket_bias(fit_rows, bias, beta, beta_high)
print("buckets:", buckets)

cur = json.loads(CALIBRATION_PATH.read_text())
out = {**cur,
       "bias": round(bias, 3), "sigma": round(sigma, 3), "beta": round(beta, 3),
       "beta_high": round(beta_high, 3), "bias_by_bucket": buckets,
       "n_labels": len(fit_rows), "fit_source": "new-prompt replays " + ",".join(map(str, games)),
       "labels": [{k: r[k] for k in ("game", "item", "t_lo", "t_hi", "t_mid")} for r in fit_rows]}
CALIBRATION_PATH.write_text(json.dumps(out, indent=1))
print(f"saved {CALIBRATION_PATH}")

155	DEFAULT_CALIBRATION = Calibration()
156	
157	
158	def _clamp(v: float, rng: tuple[float, float]) -> float:
159	    return min(rng[1], max(rng[0], v))
160	
161	
162	def calibration() -> Calibration:
163	    """Learned calibration (runs/calibration.json), clamped; the default if missing or broken."""
164	    try:
165	        d = json.loads(CALIBRATION_PATH.read_text())
166	        vals = {k: float(d[k]) for k in ("bias", "sigma", "p0", "k")}
167	    except (OSError, ValueError, KeyError, TypeError):
168	        return DEFAULT_CALIBRATION
169	    if not all(math.isfinite(v) for v in vals.values()):
170	        return DEFAULT_CALIBRATION
171	    raw = d.get("bias_by_bucket") or {}
172	    buckets = {}
173	    if isinstance(raw, dict):
174	        for name, v in raw.items():
175	            try:
176	                fv = float(v)
177	            except (TypeError, ValueError):
178	                continue
179	            if math.isfinite(fv):
180	                buckets[str(name)] = _clamp(fv, BIAS_RANGE)
181	    return Calibration(
182	        bias=_clamp(vals["bias"], BIAS_RANGE),
183	        sigma=_clamp(vals["sigma"], SIGMA_RANGE),
184	        p0=_clamp(vals["p0"], P0_RANGE),
185	        k=_clamp(vals["k"], K_RANGE),
186	        bias_by_bucket=buckets,
187	    )
188	
189	
190	def _num(x: object) -> float:
191	    try:
192	        v = float(x)  # type: ignore[arg-type]
193	    except (TypeError, ValueError):
194	        return 0.0
195	    return v if math.isfinite(v) and v > 0 else 0.0
196	
197	
198	@dataclass(frozen=True)
199	class Belief:
200	    """Lognormal belief on t: ln t ~ N(mu, sigma^2)."""
201	
202	    mu: float
203	    sigma: float
204	
205	    @property
206	    def median(self) -> float:
207	        return math.exp(self.mu)
208	
209	    def quantile(self, q: float) -> float:
210	        return math.exp(self.mu + self.sigma * _N.inv_cdf(q))
211	
212	    @classmethod
213	    def from_estimate(cls, est: dict, cal: Calibration) -> "Belief":
214	        lo, mid, hi = sorted(_num(est.get(k)) for k in ("t_low", "t_mid", "t_high"))
215	        model_sigma = (math.log(hi) - math.log(lo)) / (2 * MODEL_SPREAD_Z) if lo > 0 and hi > lo else 0.0
216	        return cls(mu=math.log(mid * cal.bias_for(est.get("_description"))), sigma=_clamp(max(cal.sigma, model_sigma), SIGMA_RANGE))
217	
218	
219	def accept_limit(belief: Belief) -> float:
220	    return belief.quantile(B_QUANTILE)
221	
222	
223	def best_charge(belief: Belief, cal: Calibration, n_grid: int = N_GRID, risk_aversion: float | None = None) -> float:
224	    """Charge maximising mean - risk_aversion * sd of the per-opponent payout, over the belief's quantiles.
225	
226	    Never above the median (a charge more likely fraud than fair is not a price, it is a bet), and an
227	    accepted over-charge pays at most CAP_MULT * t - without that cap a slowly decaying acceptance
228	    curve (k < 1) would reward charging the moon."""

"""Refit bias/beta/sigma on the REPLAYED estimates in runs/backtest/ instead of the live logs.

  pixi run python -m c2f.refit_replays

Why this exists: after a PROMPT change, the live run logs (runs/game_NN.json) still hold
estimates produced by the OLD prompt, so `c2f.calibrate` (which reads them) would fit the old
prompt's bias onto the new prompt's numbers - the 2026-08-22 prompt rewrite moved the global
bias from 1.44 to ~1.00, so recalibrating from stale logs re-poisons every price by ~40%.

Run `make replay` first (it regenerates the backtest window's estimates with the CURRENT
prompt), then this. Only the games of the current backtest window (summary.json old_games,
i.e. exactly what `make replay` refreshed) enter the fit. p0/k are kept from the current
calibration file - they come from feedback, not from estimates.

Once ~10 live games have been played on the current prompt, plain `c2f.calibrate` becomes
trustworthy again for those games and this script can retire.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import sys

from c2f import calibrate
from c2f.extract import case_labels, load_case
from c2f.price import bucket_of, CALIBRATION_PATH, PIVOT_T
from c2f.submit import ROOT


def window_games() -> set[int]:
    p = ROOT / "runs" / "backtest" / "summary.json"
    return set(json.loads(p.read_text())["old_games"])


def replay_estimates(game_id: int) -> dict[int, dict]:
    p = ROOT / "runs" / "backtest" / f"game_{game_id:02d}.json"
    if not p.exists():
        return {}
    est = (json.loads(p.read_text()).get("replay") or {}).get("estimate")
    if not est:
        return {}
    items = {int(it["index"]): it for it in est["items"]}
    try:
        descs = case_labels(load_case(ROOT / "cases" / f"case_{game_id:02d}", game_id))
    except Exception:
        descs = {}
    for i, it in items.items():
        if not it.get("_description"):
            it["_description"] = descs.get(i, "")
    return items


def labels(games: set[int]) -> list[dict]:
    rows = []
    for p in sorted((ROOT / "runs").glob("truth_game_*.json")):
        g = int(p.stem.split("_")[-1])
        if g not in games:
            continue
        est = replay_estimates(g)
        if not est:
            continue
        truth = json.loads(p.read_text())
        for i, tv in truth.items():
            it = est.get(int(i))
            if not it:
                continue
            lo, hi = float(tv["t_lo"] or 0.0), tv.get("t_hi")
            if lo <= 0 and hi is None:
                continue
            mid = float(it.get("t_mid") or 0)
            covered = bool(it.get("covered")) and bool(it.get("related", True)) and mid > 0
            rows.append({"game": g, "item": int(i), "t_lo": lo, "t_hi": hi, "t_mid": mid,
                         "covered": covered, "bucket": bucket_of(it.get("_description", ""))})
    return rows


def main() -> int:
    games = window_games()
    fit_rows = [r for r in labels(games) if r["covered"] and r["t_lo"] > 0]
    used = sorted({r["game"] for r in fit_rows})
    if len(fit_rows) < calibrate.MIN_LABELS:
        print(f"only {len(fit_rows)} labels from replays of {used} - not refitting")
        return 1
    print(f"{len(fit_rows)} labelled covered items from replayed games {used}")
    bias, beta, beta_high, sigma = calibrate.fit_bias_beta_sigma(fit_rows)
    print(f"bias {bias:.3f} (at t_mid {PIVOT_T:.0f}), beta {beta:.2f} below / {beta_high:.2f} above, sigma {sigma:.3f}")
    buckets = calibrate.fit_bucket_bias(fit_rows, bias, beta, beta_high)
    cur = json.loads(CALIBRATION_PATH.read_text())
    CALIBRATION_PATH.write_text(json.dumps({
        **cur,
        "bias": round(bias, 3), "sigma": round(sigma, 3), "beta": round(beta, 3),
        "beta_high": round(beta_high, 3), "bias_by_bucket": buckets,
        "n_labels": len(fit_rows), "fit_source": "replays " + ",".join(map(str, used)),
        "labels": [{k: r[k] for k in ("game", "item", "t_lo", "t_hi", "t_mid")} for r in fit_rows],
    }, indent=1))
    print(f"saved {CALIBRATION_PATH.relative_to(ROOT)}")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

On 2026-08-22 (after game 37) two linked changes landed:

1. **Prompt rewrite** in `c2f/llm.py` SYSTEM: honest P10/P50/P90 quantiles instead of frugal

Done. Both solutions are implemented and scored against the last 10 completed games with the real opponents. Here's the full picture.

## Results (backtest window: games 11–16, 34–37, same opponents, same stored estimates where applicable)

| Configuration | Expected net | Profitable | Top-3 | Pessimistic |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Old prompt + old calibration (baseline) | +25,273 | 7/10 | 3/10 | −127,529 |
| Old prompt + spline calibration | +36,627 | 7/10 | 3/10 | −117,948 |
| **New prompt + spline refit (final state)** | **+71,960** | **9/10** | **6/10** | −119,847 |

The verdict line for the final state: `SUCCESS — profitable in 9/10 old games, expected net 71,960`, with rank-1 finishes in games 15 and 36 and top-3 in six games (baseline managed one win, three top-3s). Most of the gain comes from the prompt fix; the calibration change is what makes it safe and self-consistent.

## What changed

**Prompt ([llm.py](c2f/llm.py))** — three targeted edits: t_low/t_mid/t_high are now honest P10/P50/P90 quantiles (the "make t_low 2–3x lower" distortion is gone); the quantity-slashing rule is scoped to *duplicated service fees only*, with an explicit statement that t applies to the line as invoiced (this alone was ~€4.5k of game-35 regret on three copper-fitting lines); the frugality slant ("claims experts are frugal, go lower") and the stale € anchors are replaced with "realistic German market gross rate" guidance, and `<market_history>` floors are now binding rather than advisory.

**Calibration math ([price.py](c2f/price.py), [calibrate.py](c2f/calibrate.py))** — the pure multiplicative bias became a linear spline in log space: slope `beta` below a €150 pivot, `beta_high` above, fitted jointly with bias and sigma by the same interval-censored MLE. The strongest validation: refit on the new-prompt estimates, **bias came out at exactly 1.00 and sigma dropped from the 1.0 clamp to 0.76** — the prompt fix removed the systematic underestimate at the source, and the sigma rail (which was forcing over-shading of both a and b) is gone.

**Guard against re-poisoning ([calibrate.py:31](c2f/calibrate.py#L31))** — `PROMPT_EPOCH = 38`: the Makefile auto-recalibrates after every game, and without this it would have refit bias ≈1.44 from old-prompt run logs onto new-prompt estimates right after game 38, inflating every price ~40%. Pre-epoch games now enter the fit only through their new-prompt replays. All 101 tests pass.

## Caveats you should know

- **The calibration is fitted in-sample** on the same 7 labelled games the backtest scores — the baseline had the same advantage, and the prompt improvement holds even under the mismatched old calibration (+73,490), so the direction is robust, but the +72k number itself is optimistic.
- **β_high sits at its 1.25 clamp** on only 98 labels. Forcing it to 1.0 costs a lot (exp drops to +28,814) so I kept the fitted value per the repo's money-gates rule, but it's worth re-checking after 2–3 more games of labels.

Done — game 38 is decrypted, replayed with the new stack, and folded into both the calibration and the evaluation. Summary:

## Results on the current window (games 12–16, 34–38, real opponents)

| Configuration | Expected net | Pessimistic | Profitable | Top-3 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| What we actually earned live (old stack) | −80,195 | — | 3/10 | 4/10 |
| New prompt + refit, β_high free (1.25) | +35,313 | −94,323 | 7/10 | 4/10 |
| **New prompt + refit, β_high capped at 1.0 (final)** | **+28,097** | **−32,869** | 7/10 | 3/10 |

`VERDICT: SUCCESS — profitable in 7/10, expected net 28,097`, with outright wins in games 15 and 36, and game 38 itself flipping from −4,274 to +495 under the cap.

## What game 38 taught us

It was the first live test of the flagged β_high risk. The model *over*-estimated two mid-size items (repair €690 vs true ≤562; drying €770 vs true ≤491), and the 1.25 above-pivot slope inflated them further — fraud-zone charges **and** fraud-accepting limits, losing on both sides. The sweep confirmed β_high=1.25 buys +7k expected for −61k worse pessimistic across the window, so I capped it.

The interesting subtlety: capping β_high **inside the MLE grid** made things worse (the fit re-balanced by pushing global bias up to 1.15; pess −82,285). The design that won is **fit-honest, clamp-at-decision**: [calibrate.py](c2f/calibrate.py) fits unconstrained (the file records β_high 1.25 as the data's best description), and [price.py](c2f/price.py) clamps it to `BETA_HIGH_RANGE = (0.35, 1.0)` at read time. The standard `make learn` → `make backtest` pipeline now reproduces the winning configuration with no manual steps — I verified that end-to-end.

Two supporting changes along the way: `calibrate.estimates()` now falls back to the replay store for a round we never played live (game 38 had no run log — a teammate seems to have submitted it from elsewhere; it shows +3,291 on the leaderboard), and case 38 is decrypted under [cases/case_38/](cases/case_38/).

## Current state and caveats

- All 101 tests pass; [runs/calibration.json](runs/calibration.json) holds the fresh fit (bias 0.91, β 0.65/1.25-clamped-to-1.0, σ 0.73, 102 labels, all new-prompt); the backtest store and summary are updated.
- Game 38's truth is still partial (272 matchup cells hadn't populated) — worth a `make truth G=38` + `make learn` in an hour or so to tighten its labels.
- Everything is still **uncommitted** (c2f/calibrate.py, llm.py, price.py, two test files, plus runs/). Given the branch got reset under me once already today, I'd commit this as a unit soon and sync with whoever is tuning RISK_AVERSION — the tree still carries their 0.40 "LOCAL TEST" against 0.55 on origin.
- Standing caveat as before: the calibration is fitted on the same games the backtest scores, so treat +28k as directional; the more trustworthy signal is the pessimistic floor improving from ~−120k to −33k and the live-vs-replay gap (−80k actual → +28k replayed).

"""Sweep B_QUANTILE x RISK_AVERSION on the backtest window, scoring stored (new-prompt)
replay estimates against the real opponents. Money only; evidence fetched once."""
import json
import sys
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(r"c:\Users\Admin\Desktop\TUM\8.Semester\Hackathon\EHL-Hackathon-template-repo")
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT))

from c2f import price  # noqa: E402
from c2f import backtest as bt  # noqa: E402
from c2f.feedback import digest  # noqa: E402
from c2f.extract import load_case  # noqa: E402
from c2f.run import merge_estimates  # noqa: E402

GAMES = [15, 16, 34, 35, 36, 37, 38, 39, 40, 41]

# fetch evidence once
evidence, estimates, cases = {}, {}, {}
for g in GAMES:
    d = digest(g)
    bt.t_bounds(g, d)
    evidence[g] = d
    rec = json.loads((ROOT / "runs" / "backtest" / f"game_{g:02d}.json").read_text())
    estimates[g] = rec["replay"]["estimate"]
    cases[g] = load_case(ROOT / "cases" / f"case_{g:02d}", g)

B_GRID = [0.20, 0.25, 0.3333, 0.40]
RA_GRID = [0.25, 0.40, 0.55]

print(f"{'B_Q':>6} {'RA':>5} | {'pess':>9} {'exp':>9} {'opt':>9} {'profitable':>10}")
results = []
for bq in B_GRID:
    for ra in RA_GRID:
        price.B_QUANTILE = bq
        price.RISK_AVERSION = ra
        tot = {"p": 0.0, "e": 0.0, "o": 0.0}
        prof = 0
        for g in GAMES:
            rows = price.price_all(merge_estimates(cases[g], estimates[g]))
            sc = bt.score(g, rows, evidence[g], "AsianSuperNerds")
            p = sc["scenarios"]["pessimistic"]["net"]
            o = sc["scenarios"]["optimistic"]["net"]
            e = (p + o) / 2
            tot["p"] += p
            tot["e"] += e
            tot["o"] += o
            prof += e > 0
        results.append((tot["e"], bq, ra, tot["p"], tot["o"], prof))
        print(f"{bq:>6.2f} {ra:>5.2f} | {tot['p']:>9.0f} {tot['e']:>9.0f} {tot['o']:>9.0f} {prof:>7}/10")

results.sort(reverse=True)
print("\nbest by expected:", [(f"B_Q {b} RA {r}: exp {e:.0f} pess {p:.0f} prof {n}/10") for e, b, r, p, o, n in results[:3]])

Done — three new games (39, 40, 41) are folded in, the eyay analysis is done, and the parameters are re-tuned on the money. Summary:

## New games

All three cases fetched, decrypted, replayed with the new stack, and their truth brackets tightened once the matchup cells populated. The window is now games 15–41. We didn't submit in any of them live (actuals: −1,186, −1,098, −1,562); the replays score +1,389, +2,503, and +22,056 — game 41 was a big-money round (OPUSMOPUS took +107k on 4 items).

## How eyay plays (from the transaction feeds, games 34–41)

Reconstructing every team's charges and accept limits against the proven t-brackets:

| Team | charge vs proven floor (median) | zero charges | implied b vs floor | rejects fair | accepts fraud | income (lower bound) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| eyay | 0.65× | 3 | 0.39× | 76% | 12% | 341k |
| Non Deterministic | 0.81× | 14 | 0.75× | 43% | 18% | 235k |
| us | 0.83× | 27* | 0.58× | 58% | 16% | 186k |

*inflated by the three rounds we sat out. eyay's formula: **charge something on every single line, shaded well under the threshold (breadth over height), and reject incoming charges hard** — wrongful rejection only costs the extra 0.5a, so in a fraud-heavy field a stingy b is cheap.

## What "leaning toward them" actually means for us

I swept B_QUANTILE × RISK_AVERSION on the backtest with our new-prompt estimates rather than copying their numbers, and the data split the lesson in two:

- **Their charge-shading transfers**: RISK_AVERSION 0.55 (more shading) dominates the teammate's 0.40 local test at every B_QUANTILE — so I reverted to 0.55, which also matches origin.
- **Their low b does not transfer**: lowering B_QUANTILE toward eyay's style *lost* money monotonically. Their slam-the-door b compensates for noisy estimates; ours are calibrated now, so trusting them and **raising** B_QUANTILE to 0.40 (accepting more genuinely fair charges) won at every risk level.

Final backtest with B_QUANTILE 0.40 / RISK_AVERSION 0.55: **expected +73,310, pessimistic total +26,874 (the only setting where even the worst-case scenario is profitable), 9/10 games profitable, 3 outright wins, top-3 in 5**. The lone negative game is 34 at −641. All 101 tests pass — one game-6 guard bound moved (950→1150) because its fixture encodes an old-prompt estimate the current prompt forbids; the rationale is documented in the test, same as the previous author did for 0.3333.

Everything is still **uncommitted** (price.py constants, the earlier prompt/calibration work, refreshed runs/). Worth committing as a unit before the next round — and your teammate should know their RISK_AVERSION 0.40 experiment reversed sign on the new-prompt estimates, in expectation and especially in the tails.

**Game by game we beat eyay 7 out of 10** (4 of those even in the worst-case scenario) — the new system is more consistent than they are, and notably we're profitable in rounds where they lose (34, 38, 39). **On total money they still win, 116k vs 73k expected — and 85k of that entire gap is one round, game 41.**

What happened in 41: a whale item ("Compensation for robbery damage", proven t ≥ 11,131). Our model estimated t_mid 8,000 (28% under the floor), and pricing then shaded down twice — the charge to 6,122 (leaving ~5k × 16 opponents on the table) and, worse, the accept limit to 4,388 because `cap_uncertain` shaved another 30% off b. We then refused everyone's fair ~7–11k charges at the 1.5× penalty. eyay charged near the true threshold and pocketed ~99k. Game 40 has the same flavor in miniature (its item 12: t ∈ [2,137, 2,880]).

So the remaining gap to eyay isn't the strategy's shape — it's **whale items**: rare, one per few rounds, but each worth more than several normal rounds combined. If you want to close that, the targeted levers would be: the `CAP_UNCERTAIN_B_SHRINK` (0.7) applying multiplicatively on items that are already our biggest downside when wrong in this direction, and a prompt/history nudge for high-value compensation items (the "stated worth binds" rule pulled t_mid to the description's anchor, but the market accepted well above it — this is the second time, game 10's watch was the same pattern). Want me to pursue that?
Yes

I'll attack the whale gap on three fronts, each gated on backtest money: (1) sweep `CAP_UNCERTAIN_B_SHRINK`, (2) sweep the β_high clamp (whales sit far above the pivot where we currently allow no lift), (3) route compensation/theft items into the `valuables` bucket so calibration can learn their bias. Here's where we stand after all the whale work, with games 42 folded in.

## Head-to-head vs eyay, rounds 34–42

| game | eyay | us (replayed, exp) | winner |
|---|---|---|---|
| 34 | −7,065 | −3,069 | **us** |
| 35 | 7,692 | 8,550 | **us** |
| 36 | 1,797 | 3,474 | **us** |
| 37 | 571 | 2,872 | **us** |
| 38 | −4,363 | 6,162 | **us** |
| 39 | −11,652 | 712 | **us** |
| 40 | 13,502 | 2,461 | eyay |
| 41 | 99,168 | 83,560 | eyay |
| 42 | −7,333 | −23,661 | eyay |
| **total** | **92,317** | **81,060** | eyay by 12% |

Before the whale changes the money gap on this stretch was dominated by game 41 alone (22k vs their 99k). Now: **we win 6 of 9 rounds and the total gap is down to 12%**, with the full window verdict at exp +81,581, pessimistic +51,054, profitable 8/10.

## What changed

- **Third spline segment**: below €150 slope 0.65, flat to €2,000, then `WHALE_SLOPE = 1.3` above — the lift now reaches whales without touching the €500–1500 mid-range (games 37/38 kept their gains, unlike the naive β_high lift which flipped them negative). Swept 1.0–1.4: expected rises monotonically to 164k at 1.4, but every whale in the window is an *under*-estimate, so the top end is extrapolation on two data points; 1.3 takes 85k of game 41's 111k ceiling while keeping b near the 4t fraud cap if a whale is ever over-estimated.
- **`CAP_UNCERTAIN_B_SHRINK` 0.7 → 1.0** (disabled): it beat 0.7 at every other setting and had cost 4.4k on game 41's whale alone, where the flag fired on the biggest item.
- Case 42 fetched, replayed, truth tightened, calibration refreshed (129 labels, bias 0.87). All 101 tests pass.

## The remaining gap is game 42 — and it's a prompt problem, not math

42 is a fine-art water-damage case, and the model priced specialist art services as ordinary trades: full restoration of the painting at t_mid 700 vs proven [2,203, 2,500), stabilisation 360 vs [915, 1,080), assessment 260 vs [439, 504). The whale lift can't rescue it because it keys on the model's own t_mid — an item the model doesn't know is a whale never crosses the knot. There was also one big miss the other way ("drying unit rental" 420 vs true ~60). Note eyay lost this round too (−7,333); Codacabana read it right (+38,677).

The fix would be a prompt rule: when the description flags a high-value/specialist object (fine art, antiques, conservators), price the *specialist* market — assessment, handling, and restoration scale with the object's value tier, typically several times ordinary trade rates. The catch: any prompt edit makes the 10 stored replays stale again, so validating it properly means a full re-replay (10 model calls, ~5 min) plus recalibration — the epoch machinery makes that safe, but it's a bigger step than a constant. Say the word and I'll run it.

Everything remains uncommitted, and rounds are landing fast — worth committing this state before the next one.

I'll add the specialist-tier rule (plus a rental-pricing guard for the other game-42 miss), re-replay the whole window with the updated prompt, recalibrate, and rerun the eyay head-to-head on the recent rounds.

def _prep(rows: list[dict]) -> list[tuple[float, float | None, float | None]]:
    """(ln t_mid, ln t_lo or None, ln t_hi or None) per usable row, computed once per fit."""
    out = []
    for r in rows:
        if r["t_mid"] > 0 and (r["t_lo"] > 0 or r.get("t_hi")):
            out.append((math.log(r["t_mid"]),
                        math.log(r["t_lo"]) if r["t_lo"] > 0 else None,
                        math.log(r["t_hi"]) if r.get("t_hi") else None))
    return out


def _loglik_prepped(prepped: list[tuple], mu: float, sigma: float, beta: float, beta_high: float) -> float:
    """Interval-censored normal log-likelihood of ln t around the spline-corrected centre
    ln t_mid + mu + (slope - 1) * (ln t_mid - ln PIVOT_T), slope = beta below the pivot and
    beta_high above (continuous at the knot). beta = beta_high = 1 is the old pure-bias model."""
    ll = 0.0
    erf = math.erf
    for m, llo, lhi in prepped:
        c = m + mu + ((beta if m < _LP else beta_high) - 1.0) * (m - _LP)
        lo = 0.5 * (1.0 + erf((llo - c) / (sigma * _SQRT2))) if llo is not None else 0.0
        hi = 0.5 * (1.0 + erf((lhi - c) / (sigma * _SQRT2))) if lhi is not None else 1.0
        ll += math.log(max(hi - lo, 1e-9))
    return ll


def _loglik(rows: list[dict], mu: float, sigma: float, beta: float = 1.0, beta_high: float | None = None) -> float:
    return _loglik_prepped(_prep(rows), mu, sigma, beta, beta if beta_high is None else beta_high)


def fit_bias_sigma(rows: list[dict], beta: float = 1.0, beta_high: float | None = None) -> tuple[float, float]:
    """rows: {t_lo, t_hi (or None), t_mid>0}. Grid MLE of (bias, sigma) with the slopes held fixed."""
    prepped = _prep(rows)
    bh = beta if beta_high is None else beta_high
    best, best_ll = (0.0, DEFAULT_CALIBRATION.sigma), -math.inf
    mus = [math.log(BIAS_RANGE[0]) + i * (math.log(BIAS_RANGE[1]) - math.log(BIAS_RANGE[0])) / 100 for i in range(101)]
    sigmas = [SIGMA_RANGE[0] + i * (SIGMA_RANGE[1] - SIGMA_RANGE[0]) / 85 for i in range(86)]
    for mu in mus:
        for s in sigmas:
            ll = _loglik_prepped(prepped, mu, s, beta, bh)
            if ll > best_ll:
                best, best_ll = (mu, s), ll
    return math.exp(best[0]), best[1]


def fit_bias_beta_sigma(rows: list[dict]) -> tuple[float, float, float, float]:
    """Joint grid MLE of (bias, beta, beta_high, sigma). Fitting the slopes jointly matters: under
    the beta = 1 model the size-shaped error inflates sigma to its clamp, which then over-shades
    every price; a single slope instead lets the mass of small bracketed items crush the rare
    big-ticket ones. Returns (bias, beta, beta_high, sigma)."""
    prepped = _prep(rows)
    best, best_ll = (0.0, 1.0, 1.0, DEFAULT_CALIBRATION.sigma), -math.inf
    mus = [math.log(BIAS_RANGE[0]) + i * (math.log(BIAS_RANGE[1]) - math.log(BIAS_RANGE[0])) / 40 for i in range(41)]
    betas = [BETA_RANGE[0] + i * (BETA_RANGE[1] - BETA_RANGE[0]) / 9 for i in range(10)]
    # beta_high is fitted UNCONSTRAINED and capped only at pricing time (price.BETA_HIGH_RANGE).
    # Capping it in the fit instead lets the MLE re-balance bias upward (1.15) to compensate,
    # which scored worse on both expected and pessimistic money than fit-honest + clamp-at-read.
    sigmas = [SIGMA_RANGE[0] + i * (SIGMA_RANGE[1] - SIGMA_RANGE[0]) / 28 for i in range(29)]
    for b in betas:
        for bh in betas:
            for mu in mus:
                for s in sigmas:
                    ll = _loglik_prepped(prepped, mu, s, b, bh)
                    if ll > best_ll:
                        best, best_ll = (mu, b, bh, s), ll
    return math.exp(best[0]), best[1], best[2], best[3]

This is a good stopping point — your ground-truth concern is exactly the right one, and it bounds how much further this tuning should go. Full picture:

## Where we stand vs eyay (rounds 34–43)

| game | eyay | us (exp) | winner |
|---|---|---|---|
| 34 | −7,065 | −391 | **us** |
| 35 | 7,692 | 6,853 | eyay |
| 36 | 1,797 | 3,879 | **us** |
| 37 | 571 | 5,974 | **us** |
| 38 | −4,363 | 4,625 | **us** |
| 39 | −11,652 | 3,797 | **us** |
| 40 | 13,502 | 17,742 | **us** |
| 41 | 99,168 | 11,603 | eyay |
| 42 | −7,333 | −7,100 | **us** |
| 43 | 815 | −1,176 | eyay |
| **total** | **93,132** | **45,807** | eyay, on game 41 alone |

**We beat eyay in 7/10 recent rounds.** Window verdict: exp +45,807, pessimistic −1,802, 7/10 profitable. The entire remaining total gap is game 41.

## What this iteration fixed

The v3 prompt (specialist-art + rental rules) initially *hurt* because of three compounding calibration bugs, now all fixed: the fit didn't know about the whale segment so it double-counted the lift (now one consistent 3-segment spline in both fit and pricing — and the MLE independently fitted the whale slope at 1.30, matching the money sweep); game 42's labels were coming from a teammate's live run with a different prompt (calibration now prefers the replay store, which is always current-prompt); and game 12's stale v2 replay was cancelling the art signal (epoch set now tracks exactly which games were re-replayed). Clean result: bias 0.98, σ 0.66, art bucket 0.76. Games 40 (−16,694 → +17,742), 37, 38, 39 all recovered.

## Your ground-truth question — yes, the trap is real, and we hit it twice today

We never see true t. `c2f.truth` recovers interval bounds per item from match outcomes (largest charge everyone paid = proven floor, smallest rejected-as-fraud = ceiling). Those bounds are *logically certain* for that round — but everything built on them (calibration bias/buckets, the market-history block, the swept constants) assumes **the next round's pricing looks like the last ten**. Concrete evidence of the trap from this session: market history says "skilled worker hours paid at least ~€667, never refused" from earlier rounds, yet in games 40/42 the same label's true t was ~€220 — same words, different quantity — and that verbatim floor pushed our estimate to 440, costing ~3.6k per game. Existing mitigations: the 10-game rolling window, bucket shrinkage, the clamps/rails, and treating history as order-of-magnitude. But every constant I tuned today is in-sample against rounds 15–43; if the organizers or the field shift the pricing regime, the calibration lags by design and only re-converges as new truth files land. That's also why I stopped tightening: the remaining negatives (42 at −7,100 where almost the entire field lost, 43 at −1,176 with still-loose truth) are within the noise this method can't reliably fix without overfitting.

## The one remaining high-value fix

Game 41's gap is **not** calibration — it's single-sample variance: the model said t_mid 8,000 for the robbery whale on one run (→ +83k) and 6,000 on the next (→ +11k), same prompt. The fix is self-consistency on dominant items: when one line carries most of a case's value (t_mid > ~1,000), sample it 2–3× and take the median. That's a change to `run.py`/`llm.py` sampling within the 60s clock, and it attacks variance rather than bias — immune to the regime-shift trap you're worried about. I'd do that next, and per-round it's worth more than everything else combined when a whale appears.

Housekeeping: all 101 tests pass, but this large uncommitted state (price.py, calibrate.py, llm.py, tests, runs/) is now several rounds of work — commit it before the next live game, and make sure whoever plays live has pulled it, since a live run on an old checkout both submits the old strategy *and* used to poison the calibration (the replay-store preference now guards against the latter).
Could we, instead of returning direct values of estimation, return a distribution instead and calculate using this distribution, with biases based on the strongest teams and

Your message cut off at "with biases based on the strongest teams and…" — so let me answer the two halves that are clear, and you can finish the thought.

## We're already half-way there — the math side is distributional

The pricing engine already runs on a distribution, not point values: [price.py](c2f/price.py) builds a lognormal belief per item, b is its 0.40-quantile, and a maximizes risk-adjusted revenue over a 200-point grid of its quantiles. What's *not* distributional is the input: the LLM's three numbers get collapsed — the median comes from t_mid alone, the calibrated σ (0.66) almost always overrides the model's own spread, and the asymmetry of the model's t_low/t_high is discarded entirely. So "return a distribution and calculate on it" is really a question about **which upgrade to the input distribution moves money**. Three candidates, in order of expected value:

**1. Mixture over samples (this is the one that matters).** Our biggest single loss driver is not distribution *shape* — it's that one sample of t_mid on a whale item swings ±65k (game 41: 8,000 one run, 6,000 the next, same prompt). The distribution-native fix: sample the model 2–3× (at least for items where one line dominates the case value), treat each sample's quantiles as a mixture component, and price on the pooled mixture. When samples agree, the mixture is tight; when they disagree, it widens *exactly where our belief should widen* — b drops on genuinely ambiguous items instead of everywhere. The pricing code barely changes (quantile of a pooled sample grid instead of a lognormal), and chunked parallel calls mean 2–3 samples fit in the 60s clock.

**2. Strongest-team-anchored bias — promising, with one trap.** Today the calibration fits against truth brackets recovered from the *whole field's* outcomes. Using the strong teams instead is attractive because their charges are dense point data while brackets are censored, and they adapt to regime shifts faster (which addresses your ground-truth worry from yesterday — their behavior *is* the current regime). But the circularity has to be handled: eyay charges 0.65× the proven floor *deliberately* — their charge is a shaded function of their t belief, not t itself. The principled version: per top team, fit their shading ratio on items where the bracket proves their charge fair (we already have this machinery in the feed analysis — eyay ≈ 0.65, Non Deterministic ≈ 0.81), then invert: `implied_t = charge / ratio`, and feed those as *soft* pseudo-labels (lower weight than real brackets) into the same interval-censored MLE. This is offline, testable with the existing backtest gate in an afternoon, and it would have pulled game 41's belief up toward what OPUSMOPUS and eyay actually charged.

**3. Richer verbalized quantiles (P5/P25/P50/P75/P95) — I'd skip.** The research we reviewed earlier (FermiEval) shows LLM verbalized intervals are systematically overconfident, so extra quantiles still need the same post-hoc calibration we already do; they cost output tokens in the clock; and they don't touch either real failure mode (location bias, sample variance). The shape refinement is worth pennies while the location and variance problems are worth tens of thousands.

## Recommendation

Do 1 + 2 together: mixture-of-samples for the belief (kills the whale variance that is currently the *entire* gap to eyay), and strong-team implied-t pseudo-labels as a second evidence stream in calibration (faster regime tracking, tighter locations). Both are gated the usual way — replay window, money verdict. One honest caveat: 2 makes us track the leaders, which converges toward the field's consensus; our edge over eyay in 7/10 recent rounds comes partly from *not* pricing like them, so the pseudo-labels should stay a minority weight in the fit, not replace the brackets.

What was the rest of your sentence — "based on the strongest teams and …"? If you meant *per-opponent* modeling (e.g., their individual accept thresholds when we set a), that's a third, separate upgrade: `best_charge` currently uses one aggregate acceptance curve, and simulating against the recovered per-team b intervals from the feeds would sharpen it. 6	moment they land so that a slow or failed full pass can never leave us with nothing, and
7	the full pass overwrites them when it arrives (last write wins on the server). The fast
8	estimate is NOT averaged or merged into the full one's numbers - over six logged games the
9	two agreed on 70 of 82 coverage calls and split the other 12 evenly, so voting bought
10	latency, not accuracy. It is used only as a cheap disagreement check: c2f.price treats a
11	coverage split or a wide t_mid gap between the two passes as a reason to price the item
12	conservatively (see c2f/price.py).
13	"""
14	
15	from __future__ import annotations
16	
17	import argparse
18	import json
19	import os
20	import sys
21	import time
22	from concurrent.futures import FIRST_COMPLETED, ThreadPoolExecutor, wait
23	from pathlib import Path
24	
25	from c2f import llm
26	from c2f.env import load_dotenv  # noqa: F401 - .env must be in os.environ before the constants below
27	from c2f.extract import case_labels, load_case
28	from c2f.price import price_all
29	from c2f.submit import ROOT, fetch_case, submit
30	from c2f.validate import invalid_indices, validate_items
31	
32	DEADLINE_S = 53.0  # clock restarts after decrypt (~1-3 s), server closes at 60 s after key release
33	FAST_TIMEOUT_S = 45.0
34	MIN_MODEL_S = 10.0  # never give the full pass less than this
35	
36	# Above this many line items the full pass is split into parallel calls of at most this size.
37	# Games 10 and 15 both shipped a fast-pass-only answer because ONE long full call missed the
38	# deadline and its whole result was lost - 6 items with 46 s left, and 29 items with 28 s left.
39	# Split, the round's latency is the slowest chunk instead of the whole invoice, and a chunk that
40	# misses costs only its own items: the rest keep their refined prices.
41	# One model, one pass (see llm.py): the call budget freed up by dropping the fast pass and the
42	# sol/luna lanes is spent on thinking instead - 10 items per call at a higher reasoning effort.
43	CHUNK_ITEMS = int(os.environ.get("C2F_CHUNK_ITEMS") or 10)  # n -> ceil(n/10) calls: 10 -> 1, 20 -> 2, 32 -> 4
44	MAX_CHUNKS = int(os.environ.get("C2F_MAX_CHUNKS") or 8)  # backstop (80 items); past that the calls fight the rate limit
45

47	def log(msg: str, t0: float) -> None:
48	    print(f"[{time.time() - t0:5.1f}s] {msg}", flush=True)
49

51	def merge_estimates(case: dict, out: dict) -> list[dict]:
52	    """Model items, validated against the parsed invoice (if the parse succeeded)."""
53	    by_idx: dict[int, dict] = {}
54	    for it in out.get("items", []):
55	        try:
56	            it["index"] = int(it["index"])
57	            by_idx[it["index"]] = it
58	        except (KeyError, TypeError, ValueError):
59	            continue
60	    # union of parsed indices and model indices: never drop a line the model saw in the raw text
61	    wanted = sorted(set(it["index"] for it in case.get("items", [])) | set(by_idx))
62	    for i in wanted:
63	        if i not in by_idx:
64	            # A POS number no chunk has priced yet. It must be a COMPLETE uncovered item, not
65	            # a bare stub: c2f.validate requires t_low/t_mid/t_high on every item, so a stub
66	            # is reported as a fatal invalid estimate and 30 of them bury the one real FATAL
67	            # in the log of a 39-item case. 0/0 is the intended ignorant placeholder (see the
68	            # submit-after-every-chunk note below), so say so explicitly and stay valid.
69	            by_idx[i] = {"index": i, "covered": False, "related": False, "t_low": 0, "t_mid": 0,
70	                         "t_high": 0, "t_if_covered": 0, "reason": "not priced by any chunk yet"}
71	    # The invoice wording rides along so c2f.price can pick a per-category bias. The model's
72	    # own output has no description field, and the category is where the estimate's bias
73	    # actually lives - one global multiplier is right for material and wrong for drying.
74	    # This must NOT read case["items"]: that list is empty since the invoice stopped being
75	    # line-parsed, and a blank description sends price.bias_for straight to the global bias.
76	    # Games 27 and 28 priced every line that way. case_labels reads the labels instead.
77	    descs = case_labels(case)
78	    # NOT setdefault: make backtest reprices STORED estimates, and the logs from games 27-29
79	    # carry "_description": "" already, which setdefault would keep.
80	    for i in wanted:
81	        if not by_idx[i].get("_description"):
82	            by_idx[i]["_description"] = descs.get(i, "")
83	    return [by_idx[i] for i in wanted]
84

86	def value_of(est: dict) -> float:
87	    """A rough per-item stake, used only to decide what gets priced first."""
88	    for key in ("t_mid", "t_high", "t_if_covered", "t_low"):
89	        try:
90	            v = float(est.get(key) or 0)
91	        except (TypeError, ValueError):
92	            continue
93	        if v > 0:
94	            return v
95	    return 0.0
96

98	def plan_chunks(indices: list[int], fast_out: dict | None) -> list[list[int]]:
99	    """Split the invoice into chunks, biggest-stake items first.
100	
101	    Order matters as much as the split. Game 10's entire 63k loss was ONE line - a
102	    stolen watch worth 7,225 - so if only one chunk had come back it needed to be the
103	    one holding that item. When the fast pass has already landed we use its numbers to
104	    rank; otherwise invoice order is all we have.
105	    """
106	    if len(indices) <= CHUNK_ITEMS:
107	        return [list(indices)]
108	    ranked = list(indices)
109	    if fast_out:
110	        by_idx: dict[int, float] = {}
111	        for it in fast_out.get("items", []):
112	            try:
113	                by_idx[int(it["index"])] = value_of(it)
114	            except (KeyError, TypeError, ValueError):
115	                continue
116	        ranked.sort(key=lambda i: -by_idx.get(i, 0.0))
117	    n = min(MAX_CHUNKS, -(-len(ranked) // CHUNK_ITEMS))
118	    size = -(-len(ranked) // n)
119	    return [ranked[k : k + size] for k in range(0, len(ranked), size)]
120	
121	
122	def _num(v) -> float:
123	    try:
124	        f = float(v)
125	    except (TypeError, ValueError):
126	        return 0.0
127	    return f if f == f and abs(f) != float("inf") else 0.0

130	def resolve_invalid_items(items: list[dict], other_by_idx: dict[int, dict]) -> tuple[list[dict], list[dict]]:
131	    """Replace every item that breaks the covered+related-must-be-positive contract (see
132	    c2f.validate), in this order: (1) the other model lane's valid estimate for that same
133	    index, (2) a positive t_if_covered from either lane. Anything still unresolved is
134	    reported as a fatal item-level error and priced as uncertain (covered=False) so pricing
135	    never receives the invalid all-zero-but-covered state (c2f.price.InvalidEstimateError) -
136	    but it is returned separately so the caller logs it as FATAL, not silently as an ordinary
137	    uncovered decision."""
138	    bad = invalid_indices(validate_items({"items": items}))
139	    if not bad:
140	        return items, []
141	
142	    by_idx = {it["index"]: it for it in items}
143	    fatal: list[dict] = []
144	    for idx in sorted(bad):
145	        it = by_idx[idx]
146	        other = other_by_idx.get(idx)
147	        if other is not None and idx not in invalid_indices(validate_items({"items": [other]})):
148	            by_idx[idx] = {**other, "index": idx}
149	            continue
150	        guess = _num(it.get("t_if_covered")) or _num((other or {}).get("t_if_covered") if other else None)
151	        if guess > 0:
152	            by_idx[idx] = {**it, "t_low": guess, "t_mid": guess, "t_high": guess}
153	            continue
154	        fatal.append({"index": idx, "reason": "no valid valuation: item invalid, other lane has none, no t_if_covered"})
155	        by_idx[idx] = {**it, "covered": False, "related": False, "t_if_covered": 0}
156	    return [by_idx[i] for i in sorted(by_idx)], fatal
157
